original_sentence: Tu Youyou has become the first female scientist of the People's Republic of China to receive a Nobel Prize, awarded for her contribution to the fight against malaria, one of the deadliest diseases in human history.
readingExamples: Tu Youyou has become the first female scientist of the People's Republic of China to receive a Nobel Prize, awarded for her contribution to the fight against malaria, one of the deadliest diseases in human history.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a country governed by elected representatives and an elected leader (such as a president) rather than a king or queen
(2) n. a system of government in which supreme power is held by the people and their elected representatives
(3) n. (used in the official names of certain countries) a state in which sovereignty rests with the citizens

posExamples.sentence: As the last colonial flag was lowered and the new banner of the young republic rose against the dawn sky, the old teacher wept openly, for he had spent his whole life dreaming of this very morning. （读后续写·历史转折·情感场景）

On behalf of the whole student body, I sincerely invite you to attend the exhibition marking the founding of our republic, where photographs and letters will bring seventy remarkable years vividly back to life. （应用文·邀请信）
A stable republic depends not merely on written laws but on citizens who are willing to shoulder their duties, respect differing voices and place the common good above personal gain. （议论文·公民责任）
Standing before the monument, the children listened as their grandfather explained how ordinary people, armed with little more than hope, had built a republic out of the ruins of war. （读后续写·代际传承）

wordForms.adjective: republican (adj. 共和国的；共和政体的 / n. 共和主义者)
wordForms.other: republicanism (n. 共和主义)｜构词法：re-(重复/相对)+ public(公共)——'公共事务'即由人民掌管，与 monarchy(君主制)相对｜大写 Republican 在美国指'共和党的/共和党人'｜专有名词大写：the People's Republic of China 三个实词首字母均大写

collocations.translation: 中华人民共和国（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Tu Youyou has become the first female scientist of the People's Republic of China to receive a Nobel Prize. （课文原句）
The revolutionaries swore to establish a republic where all were equal. （读后续写·革命理想）
The hall is devoted to the birth of the republic. （应用文·参观介绍）
As citizens of the republic, we should cherish the hard-won peace. （议论文·公民义务）
When the leader stepped onto the balcony to proclaim the republic, the vast square below erupted into cheers that echoed far into the night. （读后续写·历史场面）
A truly democratic republic is measured not by grand slogans but by how faithfully it protects the rights of its weakest members. （议论文·政治制度）

collocations.phrase: the fate / future of the republic
collocations.example: He believed the future of the republic rested squarely on the shoulders of the young, and so he devoted his final years to teaching. （读后续写·教育者情怀）

synonyms.example: From the ashes of war, a proud nation slowly rebuilt itself, brick by brick and heart by heart. （读后续写·民族复兴）
synonyms.usage: 泛指国家或民族，强调人民的共同体，不涉及具体政体；republic 特指‘共和政体’，与君主制相对

synonyms.example: The newly formed state faced enormous challenges, from a shattered economy to deep social divisions. （议论文·治理难题）
synonyms.usage: 偏向政治与法律意义上的‘政权/主权国家’，较中性；republic 强调权力来自民选、无世袭君主

synonyms.example: The founders envisioned a commonwealth built on shared duty, in which the welfare of one was the concern of all. （议论文·公共利益）
synonyms.usage: 较正式、带理想色彩的‘共同体/共和国’，多见于书面或历史语境；republic 更常用、更中性

advancedExpressions.example: In 1949, the People's Republic of China was founded, opening a brand-new chapter in the nation's long history. （短语群集中记忆）

advancedExpressions.expression: republic (n.) → republican (adj./n.) → republicanism (n.)｜re-(相对/重复) + public(公共的)
advancedExpressions.example: A republican form of government places supreme power in the hands of the people. （词族联想）

advancedExpressions.expression: not until ... did the young republic ...
advancedExpressions.example: Not until the last enemy retreated did the young republic truly draw its first free breath, and the crowd, hoarse from cheering, fell into a reverent, tearful silence. （倒装结构+拟人，续写高潮段渲染）

advancedExpressions.expression: as citizens of this republic, it is our duty to ...
advancedExpressions.example: As citizens of this republic, it is our bounden duty to protect the environment that generations before us fought so hard to secure. （倡议书呼吁段，唤起集体责任感）

advancedExpressions.expression: the strength of a republic lies not in ... but in ...
advancedExpressions.example: The strength of a republic lies not in the height of its towers but in the character of its people — their honesty, their courage and their willingness to serve. （not...but平行对比，凸显论点核心）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The people were happy when the republic was founded.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The moment the republic was founded, an ocean of people surged into the square, waving flags, embracing strangers and weeping tears in which decades of hardship and hope finally dissolved together. （读后续写·群体场面）

sentenceUpgrade.original: A republic needs responsible citizens.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It stands to reason that no republic can flourish for long unless its citizens are prepared to shoulder their responsibilities, safeguard justice and put the common good above narrow self-interest. （议论文·正式论证）

original_sentence: Tu Youyou has become the first female scientist of the People's Republic of China to receive a Nobel Prize, awarded for her contribution to the fight against malaria, one of the deadliest diseases in human history.
readingExamples: Tu Youyou has become the first female scientist of the People's Republic of China to receive a Nobel Prize, awarded for her contribution to the fight against malaria, one of the deadliest diseases in human history.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a serious infectious disease that causes fever and shivering, spread by the bite of certain mosquitoes in hot countries
(2) n. (medicine) a disease caused by a parasite carried in the saliva of infected mosquitoes, characterised by recurrent chills and fever

posExamples.sentence: Burning with fever, the young volunteer lay in the makeshift tent, and only when the doctor whispered that it was malaria did the full weight of the danger sink in. （读后续写·医疗救援·危机）
I am writing to appeal for your generous donations to help supply mosquito nets to villages where malaria still claims countless young lives every year. （应用文·募捐信）
The fact that malaria, once a death sentence for millions, can now be treated so effectively powerfully proves that persistent scientific research can rewrite human destiny. （议论文·科学价值）
Deep in the tropical forest, she treated child after child stricken with malaria, her exhaustion always melting away the instant a small hand gratefully clutched her own. （读后续写·奉献精神）

wordForms.other: malaria 为专有病名，不可数，前不加 a/an，也无复数｜'死于疾病' die of/from + 疾病名｜近义 disease(疾病统称)作上义词回指，行文可用 the disease 代 malaria 避免重复

collocations.translation: 抗击疟疾的斗争（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: ... awarded for her contribution to the fight against malaria, one of the deadliest diseases in human history. （课文原句）
Within a week two aid workers had contracted malaria. （读后续写·医者担当）
Before the cure appeared, thousands of children died of malaria each year. （议论文·全球健康）
Qinghaosu made it possible to treat malaria quickly and cheaply. （议论文·科研成果）
Travellers to the region are strongly advised to take precautions, since even a brief stay can leave one infected with malaria. （应用文·健康提示）
It is the female mosquito that spreads malaria, and so clearing stagnant water is a simple yet powerful line of defence. （应用文·科普说明）
Distributing treated bed nets is one of the most cost-effective ways to prevent malaria in high-risk communities. （议论文·公共卫生）

synonyms.example: When the epidemic swept through the town, the young nurse worked round the clock, refusing to rest even as her own strength faded. （读后续写·抗疫奉献）
synonyms.usage: 指疾病的大范围爆发或流行，强调传播规模；malaria 是具体病名，不能互换指代‘一场流行’

synonyms.example: Many once-fatal diseases have been conquered thanks to the tireless labour of scientists working far from the public eye. （议论文·科学贡献）
synonyms.usage: 疾病的统称，最宽泛；malaria 是其中一种具体疾病，行文中常用 disease 作上义词回指

advancedExpressions.expression: the fight against malaria 抗击疟疾的斗争｜die of / from malaria 死于疟疾｜contract / catch malaria 感染疟疾｜treat / cure malaria 治疗疟疾｜prevent malaria 预防疟疾
advancedExpressions.example: Her lifelong contribution to the fight against malaria saved millions of lives. （短语群集中记忆）

advancedExpressions.expression: 疟疾等疾病名多为不可数名词，不加冠词、不加复数：die of malaria / suffer from malaria
advancedExpressions.example: Hundreds of thousands of people once died of malaria every year. （不可数病名用法）

advancedExpressions.expression: little did sb. know that ... was malaria
advancedExpressions.example: Little did she know that the fever creeping through her limbs was malaria, a foe far deadlier than the jungle she had braved for weeks. （倒装+同位语，续写埋下危机伏笔）

advancedExpressions.expression: every ... could mean one fewer child lost to malaria
advancedExpressions.example: Every net you donate could mean one fewer child lost to malaria — I sincerely hope you will lend your hand to this life-saving cause. （募捐信情感升华，化抽象为具体）

advancedExpressions.expression: the conquest of malaria bears witness to ...
advancedExpressions.example: The conquest of malaria bears witness to a timeless truth: no obstacle is too formidable when human ingenuity and perseverance join forces. （bear witness to引出论点，冒号后点明主旨）

sentenceUpgrade.original: Many people used to die of malaria.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Not so long ago, malaria stalked the tropics like a silent executioner, snatching away millions of lives before any cure could reach them. （读后续写·历史悲剧）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 拟人比喻(silent executioner) + stalk动态动词渲染威胁 + snatching现在分词延展画面

sentenceUpgrade.original: Her research helped cure malaria.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It was her painstaking research, sustained through years of failure and doubt, that finally unlocked an effective cure for malaria and gave hope back to the world's most vulnerable. （议论文·人物贡献）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It was...that强调句突出研究价值 + sustained过去分词短语补充艰辛过程 + 双宾结构(unlocked...and gave)递进

original_sentence: Tu Youyou has become the first female scientist of the People's Republic of China to receive a Nobel Prize, awarded for her contribution to the fight against malaria, one of the deadliest diseases in human history.
readingExamples: Tu Youyou has become the first female scientist of the People's Republic of China to receive a Nobel Prize, awarded for her contribution to the fight against malaria, one of the deadliest diseases in human history.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. likely to cause death; extremely dangerous
(2) adj. (informal) complete; total; used to emphasise how great or serious something is
(3) adj. filled with hatred and a wish to harm; aimed at destroying an enemy
(4) adv. extremely; in a way that resembles death (e.g. deadly pale, deadly serious)

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】十足的，极度的（extreme; complete；非'致命'义，如 in deadly silence / deadly serious）
uncommonMeanings.example: We sat in deadly silence. 我们默不作声地坐着。 （课件 Reading slide 3）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 十足的，彻底的（加强语气，非'致命'义；如 deadly silence/dull/serious）
uncommonMeanings.example: For a whole hour he sat in deadly silence, and the longer he said nothing, the more certain we grew that something had gone terribly wrong. （读后续写·紧张气氛·加强语气）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 不共戴天的，你死我活的（a deadly enemy/rival）
uncommonMeanings.example: The two clans had been deadly enemies for generations until a common danger forced them to join hands. （读后续写·恩怨）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 极其，非常（多用于 deadly pale / deadly serious 等）
uncommonMeanings.example: Her face turned deadly pale as she read the telegram, and the cup slipped from her trembling fingers to shatter on the floor. （读后续写·噩耗时刻·副词强调）

posExamples.sentence: The mountaineer knew that a single careless step on the deadly ridge could send him plunging into the white silence below, so he pressed each foot down as if the whole world hung on it. （读后续写·极限求生）
I am writing to warn all residents that the chemicals stored in the abandoned factory are deadly and must never be touched under any circumstances. （应用文·警示通知）
Careless driving remains one of the deadliest threats on our roads, and no amount of convenience can ever justify putting other people's lives at risk. （议论文·交通安全）
Behind his calm smile lay a deadly determination; he had waited ten long years for this single chance, and nothing on earth would make him let it slip. （读后续写·人物意志·加强语气）

wordForms.noun: death (n. 死亡); deadliness (n. 致命性)
wordForms.other: 辨析 deadly / dead / deathly：deadly=致命的/十足的（likely to cause death），dead=已经死的/无生命的，deathly=如死人般的（deathly pale/silence，多修饰面色、寂静）｜deadly 本身既是形容词也可作副词｜-ly 结尾却是形容词的还有 lovely, friendly, lonely, lively

idioms.translation: 极其严肃，一点不开玩笑（=completely serious）
idioms.example: 'I mean every word,' he said, and one look at his eyes told me he was deadly serious. （读后续写·郑重表态）
The old novel weaves its plot around the seven deadly sins, using each character to lay bare a different weakness of the human heart. （议论文·文学赏析）

collocations.example: ... one of the deadliest diseases in human history. deadly poison 剧毒。 （课件 Reading slide 3）

collocations.translation: 【课件】默不作声地，鸦雀无声（deadly=十足的/极度的，非'致命'义）

collocations.translation: 【课件】极其严肃的（deadly 作副词加强语气=extremely）

synonyms.example: The doctors fought through the night, but the injury proved fatal. （读后续写·生死时刻）
synonyms.usage: 强调'实际造成死亡'的结果，多用于伤病、事故（a fatal accident/injury）；作表语常说 prove fatal。deadly 侧重'有致死的能力/潜在危险'，未必已造成死亡

synonyms.example: A single drop of the substance was lethal enough to kill a grown man within minutes. （议论文·安全警示）
synonyms.usage: 偏正式/科技语体，强调致死的'能力'，常与剂量、武器搭配（a lethal dose/weapon）；deadly 更口语常用，还可作加强语气的副词与形容词

synonyms.example: A deathly silence fell over the room as the verdict was read. （读后续写·凝重气氛）
synonyms.usage: 多修饰面色、寂静（deathly pale/silence/still），指'像死亡般的'外观或氛围，并非'致命'；与 deadly（致命/十足）意义不同，别混用

synonyms.example: The cliff path grew increasingly dangerous as darkness fell and the wind rose. （读后续写·险境）
synonyms.usage: 泛指'危险的'，程度较轻；deadly 程度更重，强调可能致命

advancedExpressions.expression: deadly ｜ fatal ｜ lethal ｜ life-threatening ｜ mortal

advancedExpressions.expression: however tempting ... may seem, it can be deadly

translation: 生存，存活；残存物，幸存事物
original_sentence: Thanks to her discovery of qinghaosu, malaria patients all over the world now have had a greatly increased chance of survival.
readingExamples: Thanks to her discovery of qinghaosu, malaria patients all over the world now have had a greatly increased chance of survival.
definitionEn:
(1) n. the state of continuing to live or exist, especially in spite of danger, hardship or difficulty
(2) n. the fact of a person, organisation or thing managing to keep going through a difficult period
(3) n. something that has continued to exist from an earlier time; a relic or trace of the past

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】残存物，幸存事物（something that has continued to exist from an earlier time；a survival from ...）
uncommonMeanings.example: The ceremony is a survival from 4,000 years ago. 这个仪式是四千年前留存至今的遗俗。 （课件 Reading slide 4）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 幸存者，残存物；遗留下来的旧事物（从早期留存至今）
uncommonMeanings.example: The strange midwinter ritual was a survival from ancient times, a fragile thread still linking the villagers to ancestors they had never known. （读后续写·古老习俗·文化遗存）

posExamples.sentence: Stranded on the icy peak with the storm closing in, the climbers understood that their survival now depended on one thing alone — never, ever giving up hope. （读后续写·绝境求生）
I am writing to urge our school to run first-aid workshops, since basic survival skills could one day make the difference between life and death for a classmate. （应用文·建议信）
The survival of any language rests not on dictionaries alone but on ordinary people who choose to speak it, sing in it and pass it on to their children. （议论文·文化传承）
Thanks to the new treatment, the survival rate of the patients rose sharply, and the once-silent hospital corridor began to echo with laughter again. （读后续写·医学希望）

wordForms.verb: survive (v. 幸存，生还；比……活得长)
wordForms.adjective: surviving (adj. 幸存的，尚存的); survivable (adj. 可幸存的)
wordForms.other: 词族全家桶：survive (v.) → survival (n.存活) → survivor (n.幸存者) → surviving (adj.幸存的)｜survive 是及物动词，survive the earthquake=在地震中幸存，后不加 in/from｜survive sb.=比某人活得长

idioms.example: In the harsh wilderness it is the survival of the fittest, yet the wolves' teamwork proves that cooperation can be a strength as fierce as any claw. （议论文·自然法则）

idioms.translation: 生存之战，为生存而挣扎
idioms.example: Cut off by the flood, the tiny village was locked in a desperate struggle for survival until the rescue boats finally broke through the mist. （读后续写·灾难救援）

collocations.translation: 【课件】某人的存活机会（课文原句：a greatly increased chance of survival 存活率大大提高）
collocations.example: His only chance of survival was a heart transplant. 只有进行心脏移植，他才有望活下去。 （课件 Reading slide 4）

collocations.translation: 【课件】从……留存下来的残存物/幸存事物
collocations.example: The ceremony is a survival from 4,000 years ago. 这个仪式是四千年前留存至今的遗俗。 （课件 Reading slide 4）
Some people reasonably and rightfully want to have better lives, rather than only struggle for survival. 有些人合情合理地想要更好的生活，而不只是为生存而奋斗。 （课件 Reading slide 6·完成句子原题）

collocations.phrase: a greatly increased chance of survival
collocations.translation: 大大增加的生存机会（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: ... malaria patients all over the world now have had a greatly increased chance of survival. （课文原句）
The new therapy has dramatically improved the survival rate of patients. （议论文·医学成就）
Nature runs on the survival of the fittest. （议论文·自然法则）
Thanks to the timely operation, the child's chance of survival soared, and her parents finally allowed themselves to breathe again. （读后续写·医疗奇迹）
During the wilderness camp, we learned essential survival skills, from purifying water to building a shelter before nightfall. （应用文·活动报道）
For the stranded fishermen, keeping the tiny fire alight was no longer a comfort but a matter of survival. （读后续写·海上遇险）
Only concerted global action can ensure the survival of these endangered species for future generations. （议论文·环境保护）
As the icy water rose, some primal survival instinct took over, and she clawed her way towards the faint glimmer of light above. （读后续写·危急本能）
The panda reserve was set up to secure the long-term survival of a species teetering on the brink of extinction. （应用文·环保介绍）

synonyms.translation: 【课件·同根动词】幸存，度过；从……存留；靠……为生
synonyms.example: survive sth 幸免于……/从……中艰难度过（survive the severe winter 熬过寒冬）｜survive from earlier times 从早先留存下来｜survive on sth = live on sth 依靠……生活。 （课件 Reading slide 5·动词用法，附给学生辨析用）
synonyms.usage: survival 的同根动词：survive 是及物动词，survive the earthquake=在地震中幸存，后不加 in/from（表'幸免于'）；但表'从早期留存'时用 survive from，表'靠……为生'用 survive on（=live on）。名词 survivor=幸存者。

synonyms.example: For years the little bookshop clung to a precarious existence, kept alive only by the loyalty of a handful of devoted readers. （读后续写·坚守）
synonyms.usage: 泛指'存在/生存的状态'，中性，不必然含危险；survival 强调'在危难中存活下来'，带有斗争色彩

synonyms.example: It was sheer endurance, not luck, that carried the marathon runner across the finish line long after the crowd had thinned. （读后续写·毅力）
synonyms.usage: 强调忍受艰苦、坚持到底的能力/过程；survival 强调最终'活下来/存续'的结果

synonyms.example: The persistence of the old customs, generation after generation, revealed just how deeply they were rooted in people's hearts. （议论文·传统延续）
synonyms.usage: 侧重'持续存在/坚持'的动作与过程；survival 更聚焦'度过危难而幸存'

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·序数词/被序数词修饰的词+不定式作后置定语(the first scientist to receive)
advancedExpressions.expression: 当被修饰词是序数词，或被序数词(the first/second/last/only 等)修饰时，通常用不定式作后置定语；被修饰词与不定式之间是逻辑上的主谓关系。the first female scientist to receive a Nobel Prize=第一位获得诺贝尔奖的女科学家。
advancedExpressions.example: 【课文】Tu Youyou has become the first female scientist of the People's Republic of China to receive a Nobel Prize ... 【仿写原题】Jane Goodall 是第一位研究黑猩猩(chimps)与人类之间联系的女性。→ Jane Goodall was the first woman to study the connections between chimps and human beings. （课件 Reading slide 1·仿写原题）

advancedExpressions.expression: the chance of survival 生存机会｜survival rate(s) 存活率｜survival skills 生存技能｜the survival of the fittest 适者生存｜a struggle for survival 生存之战｜the survival instinct 求生本能
advancedExpressions.example: Thanks to the new treatment, the survival rate of the patients rose sharply. （短语群集中记忆）

advancedExpressions.expression: survive (v.) → survival (n.存活) → survivor (n.幸存者) → surviving (adj.幸存的)
advancedExpressions.example: The only survivor of the crash owed her survival to a seatbelt she had almost forgotten to fasten. （词族联想）

advancedExpressions.expression: sb.'s survival hung by a thread
advancedExpressions.example: For three endless days their survival hung by a thread, and it was only the distant hum of a helicopter that finally pulled them back from the edge of despair. （比喻+时间铺陈，续写危机高潮）

advancedExpressions.expression: the survival of ... rests in our hands
advancedExpressions.example: The survival of these ancient forests rests in our hands, and I sincerely call on every student to join the tree-planting campaign this spring. （倡议书唤起责任感，rests in our hands增强使命感）

advancedExpressions.expression: survival is not merely about ... but about ...
advancedExpressions.example: Survival, in the truest sense, is not merely about staying alive but about preserving the values that make life worth living. （not merely...but递进，升华'生存'的内涵）

sentenceUpgrade.original: They tried hard to survive in the cold.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Huddled together against the biting wind, they fought for survival hour by frozen hour, drawing warmth as much from each other's courage as from the dying embers of their fire. （读后续写·患难与共）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 过去分词短语(Huddled)前置画面 + hour by frozen hour叠词式时间推进 + as much from...as平行结构升华情感

sentenceUpgrade.original: We must protect endangered animals so they can survive.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is high time that we took decisive action to safeguard endangered animals, for their survival is inseparably bound up with the health of the very planet we all call home. （议论文·环保呼吁）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is high time that+过去式虚拟语气 + be bound up with固定表达 + the very planet...home情感收束增强感染力

classPractice.question: 【课件】毕竟，并不是每个人都意识到野生动物也有思想、感情，最重要的是，有平等的生存权利。After all, not everyone has realized that wildlife has thoughts, feelings, and most importantly, equal rights ____ (survive).
classPractice.note: 课件 Reading slide 6 完成句子原题；rights to survive 生存的权利，用不定式作后置定语修饰 rights

classPractice.question: 【课件】有些人合情合理地想要更好的生活，而不只是为生存而奋斗。Some people reasonably and rightfully want to have better lives, rather than only ____ ____ ____ (为生存奋斗).
classPractice.note: 课件 Reading slide 6 完成句子原题；struggle for survival 为生存而奋斗；rather than only + 动词原形与前面 want to have 并列

classPractice.question: 【课件·语法点】仿照课文'序数词+不定式作后置定语'翻译：Jane Goodall 是第一位研究黑猩猩(chimps)与人类之间联系的女性。
classPractice.answer: Jane Goodall was the first woman to study the connections between chimps and human beings.
classPractice.note: 课件 Reading slide 1 仿写原题；the first woman + to do 不定式作后置定语，woman 与 study 是逻辑主谓关系

classPractice.question: 多亏了她的发现，全世界的疟疾病人生存的机会大大增加了。Thanks to her discovery, malaria patients now have a greatly increased ____ ____ ____.
classPractice.note: 课文原句词块 a chance of survival；the chance of survival 生存机会

classPractice.question: In the wild, it is the ____ (survive) of the fittest that decides which species endure.
classPractice.note: the survival of the fittest 适者生存；此处需名词形式 survival

classPractice.question: 新疗法显著提高了病人的存活率。（用 survival rate）
classPractice.answer: The new therapy has greatly / significantly improved the patients' survival rate.
classPractice.note: 考 survival rate 存活率 + improve/raise the survival rate 搭配

original_sentence: Born in 1930, in Ningbo, Zhejiang Province, Tu studied medicine at university in Beijing between 1951 and 1955.
readingExamples: Born in 1930, in Ningbo, Zhejiang Province, Tu studied medicine at university in Beijing between 1951 and 1955.
definitionEn:
(1) n. one of the large areas into which some countries are divided for the purposes of government
(2) n. (usually the provinces) the parts of a country that are away from the capital or major cities
(3) n. (formal) a particular area of knowledge, activity or responsibility that belongs to a person or group

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （正式）（某人的）专长范围，职责领域
uncommonMeanings.example: Judging the science project fell outside the province of the language teacher, so she humbly stepped aside and left the decision to those who knew better. （读后续写·各司其职·正式用法）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （the provinces）外省，首都以外的地区
uncommonMeanings.example: Weary of the roar of the capital, the old writer retreated to the quiet provinces, where the slow rhythm of country life gradually stitched his restless heart back together. （读后续写·归隐田园）

posExamples.sentence: The young doctor left the bustling city and travelled to a remote mountain province, where for the first time she saw how urgently ordinary people needed the skills she had once taken for granted. （读后续写·下乡奉献）
I am writing to invite you to our cultural festival, where students from every province will showcase the songs, costumes and stories that make their hometowns unique. （应用文·邀请信）
Balanced development across every province, rather than dazzling growth in a few big cities, is what truly guarantees a nation's lasting stability and fairness. （议论文·区域发展）
Born in a small coastal province, she never forgot the salt wind and the fishermen's songs, and years later they still flowed quietly through every poem she wrote. （读后续写·故土情结）

wordForms.adjective: provincial (adj. 省的；外省的；狭隘的，眼界窄的)
wordForms.adverb: provincially (adv. 在省一级；地方性地)
wordForms.other: 专有名词大写：Zhejiang Province（省名 + Province 均大写）｜province 前介词用 in：in Zhejiang Province｜复数 the provinces 常指'外省、首都以外的地区'｜province 还可表'（正式）专长范围、职责领域'：outside the province of sb.

collocations.example: Born in 1930, in Ningbo, Zhejiang Province, Tu studied medicine at university in Beijing. （课文原句）
The provincial government launched a scheme to bring clean water to every village. （应用文·政策通报）
Growing up in a mountainous province, he learned that the road to school was itself a lesson. （读后续写·成长环境）

collocations.translation: 全省各地；在全省范围内
collocations.example: News of the young hero's deed spread rapidly across the province. （读后续写·善举传播）
When the earthquake struck, rescue teams from the neighbouring province arrived within hours, tired but determined. （读后续写·八方支援）
Life in that inland province moved at a gentler pace, its people bound together by shared land and shared memory. （读后续写·乡土风情）
Many of the volunteers hailed from distant provinces, yet a common purpose knitted them into one warm family. （应用文·活动介绍）

synonyms.example: The southern region is renowned for its terraced fields, which ripple down the hillsides like green staircases into the mist. （读后续写·风景描写）
synonyms.usage: 泛指‘地区/区域’，范围灵活、不限行政级别；province 特指国家下设的正式行政区划‘省’

synonyms.example: The old district was famous for its narrow lanes, where the smell of fresh noodles drifted from every doorway. （读后续写·市井生活）
synonyms.usage: 指较小的行政区/辖区（如市辖区、街区），范围小于 province；province 层级更高、范围更大

synonyms.example: The explorers pressed on into unmapped territory, every step carrying them further from the safety of the known world. （读后续写·探险）
synonyms.usage: 强调‘领土/管辖地’或‘（陌生/抽象）领域’，范围大且偏正式；province 专指行政意义上的‘省’

advancedExpressions.expression: Zhejiang Province 浙江省｜the provincial government/capital 省政府/省会｜a coastal/mountainous province 沿海/山区省份｜across the province 全省各地｜a neighbouring province 邻省
advancedExpressions.example: Students from every province gathered to showcase their hometown culture. （短语群集中记忆）

advancedExpressions.expression: province (n.省) → provincial (adj.省的/外省的/狭隘的) → provincially (adv.)｜引申义 the provinces=外省地区
advancedExpressions.example: His provincial upbringing gave him not narrowness but a deep, unshakeable love of the land. （词义引申）

advancedExpressions.expression: born and raised in the province of ...
advancedExpressions.example: Born and raised in a quiet province by the sea, she carried its gentle rhythms wherever she went, like a song she could never quite stop humming. （分词短语+比喻，续写人物背景升华）

advancedExpressions.expression: each province boasts its own ...
advancedExpressions.example: Each province boasts its own dialects, dishes and dances, and it is precisely this rich diversity that makes our country endlessly fascinating. （boast突出特色+it is...that强调句强化主旨）

advancedExpressions.expression: not until every province thrives can ...
advancedExpressions.example: Not until every province thrives, from the wealthiest coast to the remotest highland, can a nation truly call itself prosperous. （倒装+范围铺陈，凸显均衡发展观点）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She was born in a small province and later became famous.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: From a sleepy little province few could find on a map, she rose to become a name the whole country would one day whisper with pride — proof that origins need never set the limits of a life. （读后续写·逆袭升华）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: From...介词短语前置起点 + rise to become对比落差 + 破折号引出议论点题(origins need never...)

sentenceUpgrade.original: The country should help poorer provinces.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is imperative that the nation channel more resources into its less developed provinces, for genuine progress is never measured by the prosperity of the few but by the well-being of all. （议论文·公平发展）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is imperative that+动词原形虚拟语气 + channel resources into正式搭配 + not...but平行对比升华论点

classPractice.question: 屠呦呦1930年出生于浙江省宁波。Born in 1930, in Ningbo, ____ ____, Tu studied medicine in Beijing.
classPractice.note: 课文原句词块；省名 + Province 均首字母大写，为专有名词

classPractice.question: The ____ (province) government has decided to build new schools in remote mountain areas.
classPractice.note: 此处需形容词修饰 government，province 的形容词是 provincial

classPractice.question: 用 province / region / district 填空：Zhejiang is a coastal ____ in eastern China with many rivers and lakes.
classPractice.note: 指中国的行政区划'省'用 province；region 泛指地区，district 指更小的区

translation: 广泛的；宽阔的，广阔的；概括的；开阔的
original_sentence: She completed further training courses in traditional Chinese medicine, acquiring a broad knowledge of both traditional Chinese medicine and Western medicine.
readingExamples: She completed further training courses in traditional Chinese medicine, acquiring a broad knowledge of both traditional Chinese medicine and Western medicine.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. very wide from one side to the other; large in area
(2) adj. including a great variety of people, things, subjects or ideas; wide-ranging
(3) adj. general rather than detailed; concerned with the main points only
(4) adj. (of a way of speaking) very noticeable and showing clearly where someone comes from (e.g. a broad accent)

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （口音）浓重的，地方色彩明显的
uncommonMeanings.example: The moment the old sailor opened his mouth, his broad accent rolled out like the tide, and everyone in the tavern knew at once he was a son of the northern coast. （读后续写·人物刻画·方言）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （时间）光天化日的（固定搭配 in broad daylight）
uncommonMeanings.example: That the theft happened in broad daylight, right in the middle of the busy square, left the whole town shaken and disbelieving. （读后续写·案件·加强语气）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 概括的，大体的（只讲要点，非细节）
uncommonMeanings.example: In broad terms, the project was a success, though a few details still needed polishing. （议论文·概述）

posExamples.sentence: At the top of the pass a broad valley suddenly opened before them, golden fields stretching to the horizon, and the weary travellers stood spellbound, their hardships forgotten in an instant. （读后续写·壮阔风景）
I am writing to recommend a series of lectures that will give students a broad understanding of world history, far beyond what any single textbook can offer. （应用文·推荐信）
A broad education, one that nurtures curiosity across the arts and sciences alike, matters far more than the narrow pursuit of a single high mark. （议论文·教育理念）
He greeted us with a broad smile and open arms, and in that warm moment all the awkwardness of meeting a stranger simply melted away. （读后续写·温暖初见）

wordForms.other: 词族全家桶：broad (adj.) → broaden (v.拓宽) → breadth (n.宽度/广度) → broadly (adv.)｜abroad (adv.在国外，注意与 broad 区分，a-broad)｜辨析 broad / wide：wide 指'物理上的宽'（a wide road/river，两侧距离大），broad 除物理宽外更常用于'抽象的广'（broad knowledge/agreement/smile）及庄重描写｜固定搭配 broaden one's horizons 开阔视野

idioms.translation: 在光天化日之下，公然地
idioms.example: The daring rescue unfolded in broad daylight, and passers-by froze in astonishment as the firefighter carried the child down the burning ladder. （读后续写·英勇救援）

idioms.idiom: in broad terms / in the broadest sense
idioms.translation: 大体而言，从最广泛的意义上说
idioms.example: In broad terms, success is not a single destination but a lifelong journey of learning, failing and rising again. （议论文·成功定义）

idioms.idiom: have a broad mind / be broad-minded
idioms.example: A truly broad-minded person listens carefully even to opinions he disagrees with, for he knows wisdom often hides in unfamiliar voices. （议论文·包容精神）

collocations.translation: 【课件】广泛的种类，各种各样的（broad=广泛的，include a wide range of sth）
collocations.example: a broad range of products 各种各样的产品。 （课件 Reading slide 8）
The reform won broad support from teachers and parents alike. 这项改革赢得了老师和家长的广泛支持。 （课件 Reading slide 8）

collocations.phrase: the broad appeal to the audience of all ages
collocations.translation: 【课件】广泛吸引各年龄段的观众；broad appeal 广泛的吸引力
collocations.example: The film's broad appeal to the audience of all ages made it an instant classic. 这部电影广泛吸引了各年龄段的观众，一举成为经典。 （课件 Reading slide 8）
He greeted us with a broad smile. 他咧嘴一笑迎接我们。 （课件 Reading slide 8）
The porter's broad shoulders carried the heavy load with ease. 那位搬运工宽阔的双肩轻松扛起了重物。 （课件 Reading slide 8）
He sketched a broad outline of the plan before filling in the details. 他先勾勒出计划的大体框架，再补充细节。 （课件 Reading slide 8）

collocations.translation: 【课件】从大体上说，大体而言（broad=概括的，general）
collocations.example: In broad terms, the project was a success. 大体上说，这个项目是成功的。 （课件 Reading slide 8）

collocations.translation: 对……广博的知识（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: ... acquiring a broad knowledge of both traditional Chinese medicine and Western medicine. （课文原句）
Studying abroad broadened her horizons in ways no classroom ever could. （议论文·成长价值）
The theft happened in broad daylight. （读后续写·案件）

collocations.translation: 广泛的种类，各种各样的
collocations.example: The exhibition featured a broad range of student artwork, from delicate ink paintings to bold modern sculptures. （应用文·活动报道）
When she saw her name on the list, a broad smile spread across her face, chasing away weeks of anxious waiting. （读后续写·喜悦瞬间）
In a broad sense, every act of kindness, however small, helps weave the invisible fabric that holds a society together. （议论文·社会关怀）
A broad river wound lazily through the town, its glassy surface mirroring the willows that leaned to drink from its edge. （读后续写·景物描写）
There is now broad agreement among educators that creativity deserves as much attention in the classroom as memorisation. （议论文·教育共识）

synonyms.translation: 【课件·同根副词】大体上说，广泛地
synonyms.example: Broadly speaking, the two plans point in the same direction. 大体上说，这两个方案方向一致。 （课件 Reading slide 9·broadly 用法）
synonyms.usage: broad 的同根副词，broadly speaking=大体上说，作插入语引出概括性判断；勿与 broad 混用。

synonyms.example: A wide river separated the two villages, yet a single narrow bridge had bound their hearts together for centuries. （读后续写·景物+情感）
synonyms.usage: 最常用，指'物理上的宽'（河、路、门、间隙等两侧距离大），也可指范围（a wide range）；broad 更常用于'抽象的广泛'（broad knowledge/consensus/smile）及庄重描写。注意'宽两米'只能说 two metres wide，不说 broad

synonyms.example: The scholar's extensive research spanned three decades and filled an entire wall of the library with his notes. （议论文·治学）
synonyms.usage: 强调覆盖面广、数量大、范围延伸远，偏正式；broad 侧重'范围广、种类多'或'概括的'

synonyms.example: The report offered a comprehensive analysis of the problem, leaving no important angle unexamined. （应用文·报告）
synonyms.usage: 强调'无遗漏、面面俱到'；broad 强调'广而不深、概括性'，两者程度侧重不同

advancedExpressions.expression: 【课件】broaden (1) vi. 变宽（His smile broadened. 他笑得更灿烂了）(2) vt. & vi. 增长（知识、经验）：broaden one's mind/horizons 开阔眼界；broaden access to higher education 拓宽高等教育渠道；broad-minded 心胸宽广的。
advancedExpressions.example: A promise to broaden access to higher education broadened many students' horizons. （课件 Reading slide 9·broaden 用法）

advancedExpressions.expression: wide=物理上的宽(a wide road, two metres wide)｜broad=抽象的广/庄重描写(broad knowledge, broad smile, broad shoulders)
advancedExpressions.example: The road was ten metres wide, but what impressed us was the driver's broad knowledge of every village along it. （物理宽 vs 抽象广对比）

advancedExpressions.example: A broad education broadens one's horizons far beyond any single textbook. （短语群集中记忆）

original_sentence: In the 1960s, many people were dying of malaria, and in 1969 Tu became head of a team that intended to find a cure for the disease.
readingExamples: In the 1960s, many people were dying of malaria, and in 1969 Tu became head of a team that intended to find a cure for the disease.
definitionEn:
(1) vt. to have something in your mind as a plan or purpose
(2) vt. to plan or design something for a particular purpose or person
(3) vt. to mean something to have a particular meaning or effect
(4) vt. (be intended to do / for) to be meant to serve a specified function

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】意指，意思是（=mean；to plan that something should have a particular meaning）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 意指，意思是（说话/文字的本意）

posExamples.sentence: She had never intended to leave the village, yet as the train pulled away and the platform shrank into a grey smudge, she realised that fate had quietly rewritten her plans. （读后续写·离乡·命运转折）
I am writing to inform you that we intend to hold a charity book fair next Saturday, and we sincerely hope that every student will spare no effort to make it a resounding success. （应用文·通知）
Those who intend to reform education must first understand that genuine change is measured not in grand slogans but in the quiet transformation of a single curious mind. （议论文·教育改革）
The new footbridge is intended to spare elderly residents the daily ordeal of crossing the busy road, a small design decision that speaks of great compassion. （应用文·报道·公共设施）

wordForms.noun: intention (n. 意图，打算) / intent (n. 意图，目的)
wordForms.adjective: intended (adj. 打算的，预期的) / intent (adj. 专注的；坚决的)

collocations.translation: 【课件】想要/打算让某人做某事

collocations.translation: 打算……（从句常用虚拟语气）

"I intended no offence," the stranger said, raising his hands. （读后续写·化解冲突）
What had originally been intended as a short weekend hike turned into a three-day adventure that would change their friendship forever. （读后续写·意外之旅）

collocations.translation: 专为……而设计的，供……使用的

synonyms.translation: 【课件】打算，意欲；意指（=intend by 义）

synonyms.usage: 口语中更常见，尤指'本意如此'或'无意为之'；较 intend 随意、非正式。课件 Reading slide 12 明确 intend 的'意指'义 = mean。

advancedExpressions.example: The book is intended for children, and every story is intended to spark their imagination. 这本书是为儿童写的，每个故事都旨在激发他们的想象力。 （课件 Reading slide 13）

translation: n. 提取物；选录 | vt. 提取；选录；取出；设法得到
original_sentence: She collected over 2,000 traditional Chinese medical recipes for malaria treatment and made hundreds of extracts from different herbs.
readingExamples: She collected over 2,000 traditional Chinese medical recipes for malaria treatment and made hundreds of extracts from different herbs.
definitionEn:
(1) vt. to remove or take out something, especially with effort or force
(2) vt. to obtain a substance from something by a special chemical or mechanical process
(3) vt. to get information, money, or a reaction from someone who is unwilling to give it
(4) n. a substance obtained from something else by a chemical or physical process, containing its concentrated essence
(5) n. a short passage taken from a book, film, or piece of music

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】节选，摘录（书籍/影片/乐曲的片段）；重音在前 /ˈekstrækt/
uncommonMeanings.example: The following extract is taken from her new novel. 下面这段节选自她的新小说。 （课件 Reading slide 16）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】选取；摘录；设法得到（v. 义，重音在后 /ɪkˈstrækt/；extract from sth）
uncommonMeanings.example: This article is extracted from his new book. 本文选自他的新书。 （课件 Reading slide 17）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （费力地）设法得到，逼取（信息、承诺、金钱等）；重音在后 /ɪkˈstrækt/
uncommonMeanings.example: Only after hours of gentle coaxing did the old sailor finally allow the reporter to extract from him the secret he had guarded for fifty years. （读后续写·尘封往事·套出秘密）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 拔出，取出（牙齿、异物等）；重音在后 /ɪkˈstrækt/
uncommonMeanings.example: The dentist gently extracted the aching tooth. （读后续写·就医）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 选段，节录（书籍/影片/乐曲的片段）；重音在前 /ˈekstrækt/
uncommonMeanings.example: The teacher read aloud an extract from the diary, and in the hushed classroom every student felt the weight of history pressing on their shoulders. （读后续写·课堂·历史共鸣）

posExamples.sentence: With painstaking care he extracted the tiny splinter from the child's finger, and the moment the pain vanished, her tears gave way to a shaky, grateful smile. （读后续写·救助·细节描写）
Our new herbal tea is brewed from natural plant extracts, and we warmly invite every member of the community to sample it at Saturday's charity fair. （应用文·活动通知/宣传）
True scientists do not merely collect data; they extract meaning from it, transforming a chaos of numbers into insights that push humanity forward. （议论文·科学精神）
The following extract, taken from her prize-winning essay, reveals how a single childhood memory can shape an entire philosophy of life. （应用文·报道·引用）

wordForms.noun: extract (n. 提取物；选段) / extraction (n. 提取，抽出；拔牙) / extractor (n. 提取器，抽出装置)
wordForms.adjective: extractable (adj. 可提取的) / extracted (adj. 被提取的)
wordForms.other: ★重音移位（名动异读）：动词 extract /ɪkˈstrækt/ 重音在后（提取/取出/逼取）；名词 extract /ˈekstrækt/ 重音在前（提取物/选段）——同类词还有 record, present, import, export, contract, object｜构词：ex-(向外) + tract(拉、拽，来自 tractor 拖拉机)——'向外拉出'即'提取'

collocations.translation: 【课件】……的一段节选/摘录（n. 名词，重音在前 /ˈekstrækt/）

collocations.translation: 【课件】从……中取出/得到/摘录/提炼出（v. 动词，重音在后 /ɪkˈstrækt/）
collocations.example: This article is extracted from his new book. 本文选自他的新书。 （课件 Reading slide 17）

synonyms.example: Through relentless experiments she finally obtained a stable compound. （议论文·科研·坚持）

synonyms.usage: 口语常见，尤指'引出情感/潜能/信息'；extract 更书面、可指物理或抽象的提取

advancedExpressions.expression: extract (v./n.) → extraction (n.提取/拔牙) → extractor (n.提取器) → extractable (adj.可提取的)｜ex-(向外)+tract(拉)

definitionEn:

(2) n. (in botany) a seed-bearing plant which does not have a woody stem and dies down to the ground after flowering

posExamples.sentence: Grandmother's garden was a fragrant maze of herbs, and whenever I felt lost, the mingled scent of mint and basil seemed to whisper that I was, at last, home. （读后续写·故乡·嗅觉记忆）
We warmly invite you to join our weekend workshop, where you will learn to grow common herbs on your own balcony and cook with them the very same day. （应用文·活动邀请）
The remarkable healing power hidden in ordinary herbs reminds us that traditional wisdom, far from being outdated, may hold answers modern science is only beginning to grasp. （议论文·传统与现代）
Kneeling in the dew-soaked field at dawn, the old healer gathered handfuls of wild herbs, murmuring their names like an ancient prayer passed down through generations. （读后续写·传统·画面感）

wordForms.adjective: herbal (草本的，草药的) / herbaceous (草本的，植物学用语)

A pinch of dried herbs transformed the plain soup into something that tasted of my childhood. （读后续写·味觉·回忆）
During the pandemic, many families began to grow herbs on their windowsills, finding comfort in watching something green flourish. （应用文·生活报道）
Behind the cottage lay a small herb garden where bees drifted lazily through the warm afternoon air. （读后续写·田园·环境描写）
She brewed a cup of herbal tea and pressed it gently into his cold hands. （读后续写·关怀·细节）
Tu Youyou sifted through a variety of herbs recorded in ancient texts, searching for the one that might defeat malaria. （读后续写·科研·探索）
The kitchen was filled with the scent of aromatic herbs simmering on the stove. （读后续写·家的温暖）

synonyms.example: Every plant in her garden, however humble, had a story attached to it. （读后续写·故园）
synonyms.usage: 泛指一切植物；herb 特指用于调味、药用或香味的（多为草本）植物

synonyms.example: The market stalls overflowed with colourful spices from distant lands. （读后续写·集市·异域风情）
synonyms.usage: spice 多指干制的种子/树皮/根等浓烈香料（如胡椒、肉桂），herb 多指植物的绿色叶片部分

advancedExpressions.expression: medicinal herbs 药草｜herbal medicine 草药｜herb garden 药草园｜make extracts from herbs 从草药中提取
advancedExpressions.example: She made hundreds of extracts from different herbs to find a cure for malaria. （课文原句短语群串记）

advancedExpressions.expression: herb(n.) → herbal(adj. 草本的)：名词加 -al 变形容词，同类 nation→national, culture→cultural
advancedExpressions.example: Many people now prefer herbal tea to strong coffee. （草本形容词用法）

original_sentence: When they failed to produce any promising results, Tu referred to the ancient books of traditional Chinese medicine again.
readingExamples: When they failed to produce any promising results, Tu referred to the ancient books of traditional Chinese medicine again.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. to look at a book, map, or other source in order to get information; to consult
(2) phr. to mention or speak about someone or something
(3) phr. to be about or connected with something; to relate to
(4) phr. to describe or call someone or something by a particular name or word
(5) phr. to send someone or something to another person or place for help, information, or a decision

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 查阅，参考（课文义：Tu referred to the ancient books 屠呦呦查阅古籍）
uncommonMeanings.example: When every modern method had failed her, Tu quietly referred once more to the ancient texts. （课文改写·科研·查阅）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 提到，谈及，说起（refer to sth 提及某事）
uncommonMeanings.example: In her speech she referred to her grandmother again and again. （读后续写·演讲·情感）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 指的是，与……有关（the word refers to ... 这个词指的是……）
uncommonMeanings.example: The term "greenhouse gases" refers to gases that trap heat in the atmosphere. （说明文·概念界定）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 把（某人/某事）转交/转介给（他人处理）
uncommonMeanings.example: When the young nurse could not ease his pain, she quietly referred him to a specialist across the city, unwilling to let a single patient slip through the cracks. （读后续写·医者仁心·转诊）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 把……称作，用……指代（refer to sb./sth. as ...）
uncommonMeanings.example: The villagers always referred to the old lighthouse keeper simply as "Grandpa Sea," a name that carried more warmth than any title ever could. （读后续写·乡土·称呼）

posExamples.sentence: Whenever the young researcher hit a dead end, she would refer to the yellowed notebooks her mentor had left behind, and somewhere in his cramped handwriting she always found the courage to try once more. （读后续写·传承·科研）
If you have any questions about the timetable, please refer to the notice on the board or contact the student union directly. （应用文·通知）
When we refer to "success," we too often mean wealth and fame, forgetting that a life of quiet integrity may be the truest triumph of all. （议论文·成功的定义）
In her speech she referred to her grandmother again and again, as though every lesson worth sharing had first been whispered to her in that tiny kitchen. （读后续写·演讲·情感）

wordForms.noun: reference (参考，提及) / referral (转介) / referee (裁判；证明人)
wordForms.verb: refer (refer - referred - referred; 现在分词 referring)
wordForms.other: 拼写特例：refer 重读闭音节，加 -ed/-ing 要双写 r → referred / referring；但重音前移的 reference 不双写。反义/关联：refer to（查阅） vs. consult（更正式）。

collocations.translation: 【课件】查阅笔记／查词典（refer to：查阅，参考）
collocations.example: He gave the speech without referring to his notes. （课件原句·脱稿演讲，不看讲稿）

collocations.translation: 【课件】提到，谈及（refer to = mention，说起某事）
collocations.example: We agreed never to refer to the matter again. （课件原句·同意永不再提此事）

collocations.phrase: the term refers to ... / can be defined as ...
collocations.translation: 【课件】（术语）指的是……，与……相关（下定义）
collocations.example: The star refers to items which are intended for the advanced learner. （课件原句·星号指的是给高阶学习者的项目）

collocations.translation: 【课件】把……称作，用……指代（refer to sb./sth. as sth）
collocations.example: Marcia referred to Jerry as a dear friend. （课件原句·把 Jerry 称作好友）

collocations.phrase: reference books / a list of references
collocations.translation: 【课件】参考书／参考书目（reference n. 参考，查阅）
collocations.example: There is a list of references at the end of each chapter. （课件原句·每章末附参考书目）

collocations.phrase: a reference letter / act as a reference for sb
collocations.translation: 【课件】推荐信／做某人的推荐人
collocations.example: My previous boss will act as a reference for me. （课件原句·前任上司做我的推荐人）

collocations.phrase: for your reference / for quick / easy / future reference
collocations.example: I've enclosed a copy of the timetable for your reference and future use. （课件短语·供参考）

collocations.phrase: in / with reference to ... ; make (no) reference to ...
collocations.example: With reference to your letter of the 5th, I am pleased to confirm the arrangement. （课件短语·关于来信）

collocations.translation: 查阅古籍（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Tu referred to the ancient books of traditional Chinese medicine again. （课文原句·屠呦呦查阅古籍）
Rather than guess, she referred to the dictionary and discovered a meaning far richer than she had imagined. （读后续写·求知·细节）
In his letter he referred in detail to the summer they had spent rebuilding the flooded school. （应用文·书信·回忆）
Before moving on, let me refer back to the promise we made at the very beginning of this project. （应用文·发言·衔接）
Confident in her preparation, she delivered the whole speech without once referring to her notes. （读后续写·自信·演讲）
As the chart shows, the figures refer to the number of trees planted each spring over the past decade. （应用文·图表说明）
The lawyer referred to the old photograph as undeniable evidence of the truth. （读后续写·法庭·揭示真相）
The clinic referred the difficult case to a leading hospital in the capital. （应用文·报道·医疗）

synonyms.example: Before making any decision, the wise old man always consulted the ancient almanac his father had cherished. （读后续写·传统·智慧）
synonyms.usage: 指'查阅资料'或'请教他人'时与 refer to 相近，但 consult 更正式，且可直接跟人(consult a doctor)

synonyms.example: She mentioned his kindness so often that strangers felt they already knew him. （读后续写·怀念）
synonyms.usage: 指'提及'义时可替换 refer to，但 mention 只表'顺带说起'，不含'查阅'或'指代'之意

synonyms.example: Without naming anyone, the headmaster alluded to the incident that had shaken the whole school. （议论文/读后续写·含蓄）
synonyms.usage: 指'间接、含蓄地提及'，比 refer to 更委婉、不点明；refer to 通常是明确地提及

advancedExpressions.type: 短语群·refer to 三义（课件）
advancedExpressions.expression: refer to notes / the dictionary 查阅｜refer to sth = mention 提到｜the term refers to ... / can be defined as ... 指的是
advancedExpressions.example: He referred to his notes, then referred to that plant, whose Latin name refers to its healing power. （课件三义串记：查阅／提到／指的是）

advancedExpressions.expression: reference books 参考书｜a list of references 参考书目｜a reference letter 推荐信｜for your reference 供参考｜for quick / easy / future reference 以便查阅｜in / with reference to ... 关于｜make (no) reference to ... （未）提到
advancedExpressions.example: With reference to your enquiry, I enclose a list of references and a reference letter for your future reference. （课件短语串记 reference 各搭配）

advancedExpressions.expression: refer to the books 查阅｜refer to sth 提到｜the word refers to ... 指的是｜refer to sb. as ... 把…称作｜refer a case to ... 转介
advancedExpressions.example: She referred to the ancient books, then referred to that plant as "the herb of hope." （一句串记查阅与称作两义）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·功能: 查阅/参考(可替换)
advancedExpressions.expression: refer to = consult = look sth up = turn to（查阅资料/请教）
advancedExpressions.example: When in doubt, refer to / consult / look up / turn to a reliable source. （四词可替换表'查阅'）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·refer to sb./sth. as + n.
advancedExpressions.expression: refer to sb./sth. as sth：把…称作…，as 后接名词；被动 be referred to as
advancedExpressions.example: Qinghaosu is often referred to as artemisinin in English. （被动语态'被称作'）

advancedExpressions.expression: whenever ... , sb. would refer to ... for ...
advancedExpressions.example: Whenever doubt crept in, she would refer to her mother's worn letters for the strength to carry on. （whenever 时间状语 + would 表反复习惯，塑造依赖与传承）

advancedExpressions.expression: for further details, please refer to ...
advancedExpressions.example: For further details on the registration procedure, please refer to the enclosed leaflet or scan the QR code below. （应用文固定指引句式，礼貌得体）

advancedExpressions.expression: when we refer to ..., what we truly mean is ...
advancedExpressions.example: When we refer to "a good education," what we truly mean is not the accumulation of facts but the awakening of a curious, independent mind. （下定义式论证，先破后立）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She looked at the old books again for help.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: When every modern method had failed her, Tu quietly referred once more to the ancient texts, trusting that the wisdom of a thousand years might yet light the way forward. （读后续写·科研·转折）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: When 让步/时间状语铺垫困境 + quietly/once more 副词渲染坚持 + 现在分词状语(trusting that...) 抒发信念，暗含隐喻(light the way)

sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Should 引导的倒装虚拟条件句(=If you should) + kindly 礼貌副词 + 后置定语(available at...) 提升正式度

translation: n. 实验，试验；尝试，实践 | vi. 做试验，进行实验；尝试
original_sentence: Inspired by an over 1,600-year-old text about preparing qinghao extract with cold water, Tu redesigned the experiments and tried extracting the herb at a low temperature in order not to damage its effective part.
readingExamples: Inspired by an over 1,600-year-old text about preparing qinghao extract with cold water, Tu redesigned the experiments and tried extracting the herb at a low temperature in order not to damage its effective part.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a scientific test carried out in order to study what happens and to gain new knowledge
(2) n. the process of trying out a new idea, method, or activity to see how good or effective it is
(3) vi. to perform a scientific test in order to learn something or prove a theory
(4) vi. to try out new ideas, methods, or ways of doing things

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 科学实验，试验（课文义：redesign the experiments 重新设计实验）
uncommonMeanings.example: Tu redesigned the experiments to protect the herb's effective part. （课文改写·科研）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 做试验，进行实验；（大胆地）尝试新方法（experiment with sth）
uncommonMeanings.example: Great minds are not afraid to experiment. （议论文·创新精神）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （生活/态度上的）新尝试，大胆试验
uncommonMeanings.example: Leaving the city for a remote mountain school was, she admitted, a reckless experiment in living — yet it turned out to be the truest decision of her life. （读后续写·人生抉择·大胆尝试）

posExamples.sentence: The experiment had failed for the two-hundredth time, yet as smoke curled from the flask, Tu wiped her brow and reached, without a word, for a fresh set of test tubes. （读后续写·科研·坚持不懈）
We are organising a series of hands-on science experiments for younger students, and we sincerely hope that volunteers with a passion for chemistry will sign up before Friday. （应用文·招募通知）
Great minds are not afraid to experiment, for they understand that every failure quietly carves out the path toward the next discovery. （议论文·创新精神）
That summer we experimented with growing vegetables on the rooftop, and though half of them withered, the joy of the first ripe tomato made every effort worthwhile. （读后续写·成长·尝试）

wordForms.noun: experiment / experimentation (实验过程) / experimenter (实验者)
wordForms.other: 注意名词与动词同形 experiment，作动词时读音重音略后移。派生：experiment + -al → experimental（形容词，an experimental drug 试验药物）；+ -ally → experimentally。搭配辨析：experiment with sth（用某物做实验/尝试） vs. experiment on sb.（在某人身上做实验）。

collocations.phrase: do / conduct / perform / carry out an experiment
collocations.translation: 【课件】做实验，进行实验（四个动词均可搭 experiment）
collocations.example: Many scientists do this experiment to prove the theory. （课件搭配·做实验）
Many people do not like the idea of experiments on animals. （课件原句·反对动物实验）

collocations.translation: 【课件】在……方面的实践／尝试（n. 实践，尝试）
collocations.example: the country's bold experiment in democracy （课件短语·民主实践）

collocations.translation: 【课件】尝试某事；用某物做实验（experiment vi.）
collocations.example: The young film-makers are experimenting with new filming techniques. （课件原句·尝试新拍摄技术）
Experimenting on mice can throw light on the disease. （课件原句·在老鼠身上做试验以了解疾病）

collocations.translation: 重新设计实验（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Tu redesigned the experiments and tried extracting the herb at a low temperature. （课文原句·重新设计实验）

collocations.phrase: do / carry out / conduct an experiment
collocations.translation: 做实验，进行试验（高考高频搭配）
collocations.example: Night after night the team carried out experiment after experiment, refusing to let exhaustion win. （读后续写·科研·毅力）
Before drawing any conclusion, the scientists performed the experiment a hundred times over. （议论文·严谨）
The scientific experiment finally confirmed what the ancient text had hinted at all along. （读后续写·古今呼应）
A single successful experiment, born of a thousand failed ones, changed the course of medicine forever. （议论文·成功与失败）
Inspired by an ancient recipe, she redesigned the experiment from the ground up. （读后续写·灵感·创新）
Truth in science is established not by authority but through patient experiment. （议论文·科学精神）
Refusing to experiment on others first, the brave researcher tested the new drug on herself. （读后续写·科研·牺牲精神）

synonyms.example: The new vaccine passed every clinical trial with flying colours. （应用文·科技报道）
synonyms.usage: trial 侧重'为检验效果/安全而进行的正式测试'(尤指临床、法律)；experiment 侧重'为探索未知、验证理论的科学试验'

synonyms.example: Adversity is the truest test of a person's character. （议论文·品格）
synonyms.usage: test 泛指各种'检验、考验'，范围最广、最口语；experiment 特指有系统、有变量控制的探究性试验

synonyms.example: She decided to try out the new study method before recommending it to her classmates. （读后续写·学习·尝试）
synonyms.usage: try out 口语化，指'实际用一用看行不行'，非正式；experiment 更正式、更强调探索与验证过程

advancedExpressions.expression: do / conduct / perform / carry out an experiment 做实验｜experiments on animals 动物实验｜experiment with sth 尝试｜experiment on sth 在…上做实验｜experiment in sth 在…的实践

original_sentence: When there was no research equipment, they had to extract herbs using household water containers.

definitionEn:
(1) n. all the people who live together in one house or flat, considered as a unit
(2) adj. relating to a home and the people who live there; used in or connected with the home
(3) adj. (of a name/word) very familiar and known to almost everyone

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 家用的，家庭的（课文义：household water containers 家用盛水容器）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 一家人，一户（同住一处、作为一个居住/经济单位的人）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 家喻户晓的（常见于 a household name / word）
uncommonMeanings.example: Overnight, the shy street violinist whose video had gone viral became a household name, and strangers now stopped him in the market just to shake his hand. （读后续写·一夜成名·命运转折）

In our upcoming green campaign, we encourage each household to sort waste, reuse plastic bags, and switch off idle appliances, for small habits at home add up to a mighty force. （应用文·倡议书）
Statistics reveal that the average household now spends far more hours before screens than in conversation, a silent shift that is quietly reshaping family bonds. （议论文·科技与家庭）

wordForms.other: 构词法：house(房子) + hold → household（合成词，'一屋子人'即家庭）；+ -er → householder（户主）。词性双重：作名词'一家人'（可数，every household），作形容词'家用的'（household appliances）。辨析：household（居住/经济单位，可含非亲属） vs. family（血缘家人）。

definitionEn:
(1) n. a box, bottle, jar, etc. in which something can be stored or transported
(2) n. a very large metal or wooden box of a standard size, used for transporting goods by ship, road, or rail
(3) n. (computing) a lightweight, standalone package that holds an application and everything it needs to run

uncommonMeanings.example: At the vast, silent port, thousands of steel containers were stacked like a giant's discarded building blocks. （读后续写·港口·童真视角）

To reduce plastic waste on campus, we suggest that every student bring a reusable container for lunch instead of relying on disposable boxes. （应用文·倡议书）
The invention of the standardized shipping container may seem humble, yet economists argue it transformed global trade more profoundly than many a celebrated technology. （议论文·科技与经济）

wordForms.noun: container (容器；集装箱) / containment (遏制，围堵)
wordForms.other: 构词法：contain(v. 容纳) + -er → container（容纳东西的物件=容器）。同族记忆：contain 包含/容纳、container 容器、containment 遏制。搭配区分：container（普通容器）与 container ship（集装箱船）。

collocations.translation: 家用盛水容器（课文原句词块）

The enormous container ship glided silently into the harbour, dwarfing the fishing boats that bobbed alongside. （读后续写·环境描写）
The archaeologists stored the fragile scroll in an airtight container to shield it from the corrosive touch of the air. （读后续写·考古发现）
She carefully poured the leftover soup into a glass container and tucked it into the fridge for tomorrow. （读后续写·居家）
Carrying a reusable container to the canteen is a tiny gesture, yet if we all do it, mountains of plastic waste will simply vanish. （应用文·环保倡议）

original_sentence: The trials on patients were likely to be postponed because they did not have sufficient safety data.
readingExamples: The trials on patients were likely to be postponed because they did not have sufficient safety data.
definitionEn:
(1) vt. to arrange for an event, meeting, etc. to take place at a later time or date than originally planned; to delay
(2) vt. to put off doing something until a later time

posExamples.sentence: As the storm howled against the windows, the captain reluctantly decided to postpone the voyage, knowing that a rash departure might cost every soul aboard their life. （读后续写·抉择时刻）
Due to the sudden downpour, we regret to inform you that the outdoor sports meeting has been postponed until next Friday; further details will be announced in due course. （应用文·通知）
Some students habitually postpone their revision until the eve of the exam, yet such procrastination, however tempting, almost always breeds panic rather than progress. （议论文·拖延与自律）

wordForms.other: 构词法：post-（在…之后）+ pone（放置，源自拉丁语 ponere）→ postpone（放到以后=推迟）。名词 postpone + -ment → postponement。关键考点：postpone 后必须接名词或动名词（postpone doing sth），不接不定式；= put off doing sth。

collocations.translation: 【课件】把某事推迟到……（postpone 后接名词或动名词）
collocations.example: We'll have to postpone the meeting until next week. （课件原句·把会议推迟到下周）

collocations.translation: 【课件】延迟，延期（= put off / delay）
collocations.example: The trials on patients were likely to be postponed because they did not have sufficient safety data. （课件原句·因数据不足而延期）

collocations.phrase: the trials were likely to be postponed
collocations.translation: 试验很可能被推迟（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: The trials on patients were likely to be postponed because they did not have sufficient safety data. （课文原句·因数据不足而延期）

collocations.phrase: postpone doing sth (= put off doing sth)
collocations.translation: 推迟做某事（高频考点，postpone 后接动名词）
collocations.example: He kept postponing telling his parents the truth, and with every passing day the secret weighed more heavily on his heart. （读后续写·心理描写）

collocations.phrase: be postponed due to / because of sth
collocations.example: The final trials were postponed because of insufficient safety data, a delay that tested the researchers' patience to the limit. （读后续写·科研）

collocations.phrase: postpone sth until / to a later date
collocations.example: The organizers postponed the charity concert to a later date so that more volunteers could take part. （应用文·活动通知）
When funding dried up, the ambitious project was postponed indefinitely, and the once-buzzing office fell silent. （读后续写·挫折）
Unable to weigh the two offers, she chose to postpone the decision, hoping that a clearer head would come with the morning. （读后续写·两难）
In view of the technical faults, the committee agreed to postpone the submission deadline by one week. （应用文·通知）

synonyms.example: Heavy fog delayed all flights, leaving weary travellers slumped across the terminal benches. （读后续写·机场）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：delay 既可指主动推迟，也可指被动耽搁、拖延（含负面意味），主语可为人或事；postpone 通常是有计划地、正式地改期，语气更中性、更正式。

synonyms.example: Don't put off till tomorrow what you can accomplish today, the old proverb warns. （议论文·引谚语）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：put off 是口语化短语，常含“因不情愿而拖延”的意味；postpone 更正式书面，适用于会议、比赛、考试等正式安排的改期。

synonyms.example: The trial was suspended the moment new evidence surfaced in the courtroom. （读后续写·法庭）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：suspend 强调暂时中止一项正在进行的活动（比赛、会议、职务等），可能不定期；postpone 只是把尚未开始的事推到以后的时间，仍会照常进行。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·功能: 推迟(可替换)（课件）
advancedExpressions.expression: postpone = put off = delay（把…推迟）：postpone 正式书面，put off 口语，delay 兼指'耽搁'
advancedExpressions.example: The meeting was postponed / put off / delayed until next week. （课件三词此处可替换）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·postpone (doing) sth to / until（课件）
advancedExpressions.expression: postpone (doing) sth to / until ...：postpone 后接名词或动名词，不接 to do；改期到某时用 to / until
advancedExpressions.example: We'll have to postpone the meeting until next week. （课件原句·推迟到下周；postpone 后不接不定式）

advancedExpressions.expression: postpone doing sth 推迟做某事｜be postponed until ... 推迟到｜postpone the deadline 延长截止期｜postpone indefinitely 无限期推迟
advancedExpressions.example: They postponed announcing the result and postponed the trials until more data came in. （一句串记两种搭配）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·功能: 推迟(可替换)
advancedExpressions.expression: postpone = put off = delay = defer（把…推迟）：postpone/defer 正式，put off 口语，delay 兼指'耽搁'
advancedExpressions.example: The meeting was postponed / put off / delayed until Friday. （三词此处可替换）

advancedExpressions.expression: postpone doing sth：postpone 后接动名词，不接 to do；同类 put off / avoid / consider / finish 后均接 -ing
advancedExpressions.example: Don't postpone doing what can be done today. （postpone 后接动名词 doing，非 to do）

advancedExpressions.expression: reluctant though sb. was, ... had to be postponed
advancedExpressions.example: Reluctant though the whole team was, the expedition had to be postponed, for no dream, however bright, is worth a single needless life. （倒装让步 + 格言式收束，凸显理性与责任）

advancedExpressions.expression: we regret to inform you that ... has been postponed
advancedExpressions.example: We regret to inform you that, owing to unforeseen circumstances, the graduation ceremony has been postponed to a date to be confirmed. （通知类固定套路，得体委婉）

advancedExpressions.expression: to postpone ... is, in essence, to ...
advancedExpressions.example: To postpone what must be done is, in essence, to surrender the present to the tyranny of the future; the disciplined mind acts today. （下定义式论断，强化说理力度）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The trials had to be postponed because there was not enough safety data.

original_sentence: The trials on patients were likely to be postponed because they did not have sufficient safety data.
readingExamples: The trials on patients were likely to be postponed because they did not have sufficient safety data.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. as much as is needed for a particular purpose; enough
(2) adj. (formal) adequate in quantity or degree to meet a requirement, often in the phrase sufficient for/to do sth

posExamples.sentence: By the time the rescue team arrived, the stranded climbers had barely sufficient food to last another day, yet their eyes still burned with a stubborn refusal to give up. （读后续写·绝境求生）
To ensure the smooth running of the book fair, please make sure sufficient volunteers are on duty at each booth throughout the day. （应用文·通知）
Good intentions alone are never sufficient to bring about lasting change; they must be matched by concrete action and unwavering perseverance. （议论文·知与行）

wordForms.adjective: sufficient（足够的）/ insufficient（不足的，反义）/ self-sufficient（自给自足的）
wordForms.other: 反义词 insufficient（in- 否定前缀 + sufficient）；suffice it to say (that) ... = 只需说……就够了（固定表达）；构词 suf-(=sub-,在下)+fic-(做)+-ient(形容词后缀)，本义“做得够到底下的量”

idioms.idiom: sufficient unto the day (is the evil thereof)
idioms.translation: 一天的难处一天当（不必为明天过分忧虑，出自《圣经》）
idioms.example: "Sufficient unto the day," the old farmer murmured, wiping his brow; he had learned long ago not to borrow tomorrow's troubles. （读后续写·乡村智慧·人物刻画）

collocations.example: These reasons are not sufficient to justify the ban. （课件原句·理由不足以支持禁令）

collocations.translation: 【课件】不充分的，不足的（反义词）

synonyms.translation: 足够的，够用的（但未必优质）

advancedExpressions.expression: sufficient 足够的｜insufficient 不足的(opp.)｜self-sufficient 自给自足的｜sufficiency n. 足量｜suffice v. 足够
advancedExpressions.example: A self-sufficient farm produces a sufficiency of food, so its supplies are never insufficient. （课件同族词串记：sufficient / insufficient / self-sufficient / sufficiency）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·功能: 足够(课件)

advancedExpressions.expression: be sufficient for sth / be sufficient to do sth / more than sufficient / prove sufficient / suffice it to say that ...

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·表示“足够”(可替换)
advancedExpressions.expression: sufficient ≈ enough ≈ adequate ≈ ample（均可表“足够”，正式度 ample/sufficient > adequate > enough）
advancedExpressions.example: We had sufficient / enough / adequate / ample time to finish. （四词在此句均可互换，仅语体正式度不同）

advancedExpressions.expression: sufficient → insufficient（不足的）；辅音同化前缀 in- 在此保持原形

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·necessary but not sufficient 逻辑术语

advancedExpressions.expression: please ensure that sufficient ... is/are provided

advancedExpressions.expression: ... is necessary but not sufficient

sentenceUpgrade.original: They did not have enough safety data, so the trials might be delayed.

sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 现在分词短语作原因状语(Lacking...) + 冒号引出两难抉择 + or 并列凸显矛盾 + slip away 拟人化时间流逝

original_sentence: The trials on patients were likely to be postponed because they did not have sufficient safety data.
readingExamples: The trials on patients were likely to be postponed because they did not have sufficient safety data.
definitionEn:
(1) n. facts or information, especially when examined and used to find out things or to make decisions
(2) n. (computing) information in a form that can be stored and processed by a computer
(3) n. (technical) the plural of datum: individual pieces of information

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （技术/严格语法）datum 的复数形式，指用于推理的一条条既定事实、论据前提（正式语境可作复数，谓语用 are；日常与计算机语境常作不可数，谓语用 is）
uncommonMeanings.example: In strict scientific writing, the data are still incomplete, so no firm conclusion can be drawn. （议论文·数据尚不完整，谓语用 are）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （哲学/逻辑）已知资料，论据的前提（datum 的复数，指据以推理的既定事实）
uncommonMeanings.example: The philosopher reminded his students that even the most elegant argument crumbles if the data on which it rests are false. （议论文·逻辑思辨·前提为真）

posExamples.sentence: Hunched over the dim monitor at midnight, the young scientist stared at the flood of data, and suddenly her heart leapt — hidden in the endless numbers lay the pattern she had chased for years. （读后续写·科研突破）
Before we launch the campus recycling programme, I suggest we collect accurate data on how much waste each building produces, so that our plan rests on facts rather than guesswork. （应用文·建议信）
In an age drowning in information, the ability to interpret data critically — to tell signal from noise — has become one of the most valuable skills a citizen can possess. （议论文·信息素养）

wordForms.noun: data / datum / database（数据库）/ dataset（数据集）
wordForms.other: datum 为单数原形（源自拉丁语，较少用），data 为其复数；现代英语中 data 在计算机、日常语境常作不可数名词，谓语用单数(The data is...)，在正式科学论文中仍可作复数(The data are...)；计量单条用 a piece of data / an item of data

collocations.translation: 充足的安全数据（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: They did not have sufficient safety data, so the trials were likely to be postponed. （课文原句词块·安全数据不足）
For six long months the team gathered data in the freezing wilderness, unwilling to let a single measurement slip. （读后续写·科考）

collocations.translation: 一条/一项数据（data 作可数时用 a piece of 计量）
collocations.example: Not a single piece of data was allowed to be recorded without a second check. （14词·严谨核对）
Careful data analysis finally revealed the hidden pattern no one had noticed. （11词·分析显现规律）
Only after analysing the data with painstaking care did they dare to announce their startling discovery. （读后续写·科研严谨）
The trials had to wait until sufficient safety data confirmed that the new drug posed no hidden danger. （读后续写·医学试验）
The latest data reveals that students who read for pleasure consistently outperform their peers in writing. （议论文·阅读的价值）
Without reliable data, even the boldest theory is little more than an educated guess. （议论文·实证精神）
A single modern phone can store more data than an entire library did a century ago. （议论文·科技变迁）
As our lives move online, data protection has become a concern no responsible government can afford to ignore. （议论文·数字时代）
Remember to back up your data regularly, for a single crash can erase months of hard work in an instant. （应用文·温馨提示）

synonyms.example: The librarian patiently helped the anxious student sift through mountains of information to find the one fact he needed. （读后续写·图书馆）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：information 是不可数的总称，泛指各类信息，计量用 a piece of information；data 侧重可测量、可统计、可供分析的事实与数字，计量用 a piece of data，更常见于科研、统计、计算机语境。

synonyms.example: The report's alarming statistics on plastic pollution left the whole audience in stunned silence. （议论文·环保）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：statistics 特指经过统计整理的数量化数据，恒作复数用，常用于呈现结果；data 范围更广，既包括未加工的原始资料，也包括统计结果。

synonyms.example: The sales figures for the charity sale far exceeded everyone's hopes. （应用文·活动报道）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：figures 口语化，专指具体数字（金额、数量等），恒为复数；data 更正式、更学术，涵盖数字之外的各类事实性资料。

advancedExpressions.expression: buried in the data lay ...

advancedExpressions.expression: let the data speak for itself / base ... on solid data

sentenceUpgrade.original: They did not have enough safety data, so the trials were likely to be postponed.

classPractice.note: 考点：正式科学写作中 data 作 datum 的复数，谓语用 are。

original_sentence: To speed up the process and ensure its safety, Tu and her team volunteered to test qinghao extract on themselves first.
readingExamples: To speed up the process and ensure its safety, Tu and her team volunteered to test qinghao extract on themselves first.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. v. to move or happen faster, or to make something move or happen faster
(2) phr. v. to increase the rate or pace at which a process or activity develops
(3) phr. v. (of a machine, vehicle or person) to begin to travel or work at a greater speed

posExamples.sentence: As the deadline drew nearer, Tu's team decided to speed up their experiments, working late into the freezing nights until exhaustion blurred the numbers before their eyes. （读后续写·科研奋斗）
To speed up the review of donated books, we sincerely invite ten more volunteers to join our library committee this weekend. （应用文·招募通知）
Blindly speeding up economic growth at the expense of the environment may bring short-term wealth, yet it ultimately robs future generations of a habitable planet. （议论文·发展与环保）
The old train groaned, then began to speed up, and soon the platform where her mother stood waving shrank into a tiny, fading dot. （读后续写·离别场景）

wordForms.noun: speed（速度；n.加速可用 speedup 一词）
wordForms.verb: speed（v. 疾行，加速；speed up 短语）
wordForms.other: 反义短语 slow down（减速）；speed up 中 speed 作动词，过去式常用 speeded up（表“加速”这一层义时用规则形式），而 speed 表“超速/疾驰”时过去式为 sped；比较：pick up speed = 加速（另一表达）

idioms.translation: （使）加速，加快（可及物“加快某事”，也可不及物“自身加速”）；反义 slow down
idioms.example: The train slowed down at the bend, then speeded up again as the track straightened out. （对照 speed up 与反义 slow down）

collocations.translation: 【课件】（使）加速；加快（可及物“加快某事”，也可不及物“自身加速”）；反义短语 slow down 减速、慢下来
collocations.example: The truck speeded up going down the hill. 卡车在下山时加快了速度。（课件·Reading）
How did the accident come about since he drove at a speed of sixty miles per hour? （课件·完成句子原句）

collocations.phrase: at high / low / full / top speed
collocations.translation: 【课件】以高速 / 低速 / 全速 / 最快速度
collocations.example: The racing car swept past us at full speed, and in a heartbeat it was gone. （课件·speed 相关短语）
As we laughed over old photos, the whole afternoon seemed to speed by in a single breath. （课件·speed by 时光飞逝）

collocations.translation: 【课件】减速，慢下来（speed up 的反义短语）

collocations.translation: 为了加快进程（课文原句词块）

By adopting the new assembly line, the factory managed to speed up production without ever compromising on quality. （议论文·效率论证）
Gentle exercise and a balanced diet can greatly speed up recovery after a serious illness. （应用文·健康建议）
"Let me help you speed things up," the old carpenter said, rolling up his sleeves as the boy struggled with the stubborn nails. （读后续写·助人对话）

Sensing the approaching storm, she speeded up her pace until the umbrella trembled violently in her grip. （读后续写·环境渲染）
The invention of the printing press significantly speeded up the spread of knowledge across Europe. （议论文·历史论证）

synonyms.example: The reform accelerated the modernization of the countryside far beyond anyone's expectations. （议论文·社会发展）
synonyms.usage: 较正式，一个单词动词，可及物可不及物，多用于书面语和议论文，常搭配抽象过程（growth, decline, change）；speed up 是短语动词，更口语化，叙事和应用文均可。

synonyms.example: Her heartbeat quickened as footsteps echoed down the empty corridor. （读后续写·紧张心理）
synonyms.usage: 偏文学性，常用于心跳、脉搏、步伐等，续写渲染情绪时尤佳；speed up 更中性通用。

synonyms.example: Ignoring warnings only hastened the company's collapse. （议论文·因果论证）
synonyms.usage: 正式，强调促使某事更快发生（常含负面结果），书面论证中显文采；speed up 语气中性。

advancedExpressions.type: 短语群·speed / slow 反义对

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·表示“加速”(可替换)
advancedExpressions.expression: speed up ≈ accelerate ≈ quicken ≈ hasten（均表“加快”，正式度 accelerate/hasten > quicken > speed up）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·及物/不及物两用 + 代词位置

advancedExpressions.expression: with every ... , sb. speeded up, determined to ...

advancedExpressions.expression: in order to speed up ..., I would suggest that ...

classPractice.note: 课件原题：at a speed of + 具体速度，介词固定用 at、of。
