translation: 政治家，从政者；投机钻营者
original_sentence: Benjamin Franklin was a famous scientist, writer, printer, inventor and politician.
readingExamples: Benjamin Franklin was a famous scientist, writer, printer, inventor and politician.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a person whose job is concerned with politics, especially as an elected member of a government
(2) n. someone who is skilled at dealing with people and getting things done through influence and persuasion
(3) n. (disapproving) a person who cares more about personal gain and manoeuvring than about principles

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (贬)工于心计、善于钻营的人；玩弄权术者
uncommonMeanings.example: He was less a leader than a politician at heart, always sensing which way the wind blew and bending his words to please whoever held power that day. （读后续写·人物讽刺·世故）

posExamples.sentence: As a boy, he had listened, wide-eyed, to the old politician's speeches on the radio, never once dreaming that one day he too would stand before a cheering crowd. （读后续写·梦想的种子）
We are honoured to invite a respected local politician to deliver the opening speech at our youth leadership forum next month. （应用文·邀请信）
A truly great politician is remembered not for the power he once held, but for the lasting good he did for ordinary people. （议论文·领导力/品格）
Franklin was far more than a politician; he was at once a scientist, a writer and an inventor whose curiosity knew no bounds. （读后续写/说明·人物介绍）

wordForms.noun: politician (政治家) / politics (政治；政治学) / policy (政策，方针)
wordForms.other: 词族辨析：politics 政治(学) → political 政治的 → politician 从政者；注意 policy(政策) 拼写与词义均不同，勿与 politics 混淆

collocations.phrase: a scientist, writer, printer, inventor and politician
collocations.translation: 科学家、作家、印刷商、发明家兼政治家（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Benjamin Franklin was a famous scientist, writer, printer, inventor and politician. （课文原句）
A prominent politician of her generation, she devoted her life to improving education. （议论文·人物评价）
The novel exposes how a corrupt politician can gradually lose sight of the very people he once vowed to serve. （议论文·社会批判）

collocations.translation: 正直的/受人尊敬的政治家
collocations.example: In an age of empty promises, an honest politician who keeps his word earns a loyalty no amount of money can buy. （议论文·诚信主题）
Unlike the smooth career politicians around him, he spoke plainly and admitted his mistakes without hesitation. （读后续写·人物对比）
After decades of teaching, she turned politician, determined to fight for the schools she had served all her life. （读后续写·人生转折）
The townspeople gathered in the square to elect a politician they could finally trust to keep his promises. （读后续写·社区场景）
Even the most seasoned politician in the room fell silent as the young activist laid bare an uncomfortable truth. （读后续写·辩论场面）

synonyms.example: History would remember him not as a mere politician but as a statesman who put his nation above himself. （议论文·历史评价）
synonyms.usage: statesman 是纯褒义，指有远见卓识、德高望重的政治领袖；politician 中性偏贬，日常泛指从政者，有时暗含'耍手腕'之意

synonyms.example: A good leader listens more than he speaks, and acts long before he is asked. （议论文·领导力）
synonyms.usage: leader 泛指各领域的领导者(不限政界)，强调引领与担当；politician 特指政界人物，侧重其从政身份

synonyms.example: A local official visited the flood-stricken village to oversee the relief work in person. （应用文/记叙·公职人员）
synonyms.usage: official 指担任具体公职、执行政务的官员(未必经选举)；politician 更强调从事政治活动、常经选举产生的政界人士

advancedExpressions.expression: one day he too would stand where the politician now stood
advancedExpressions.example: Gazing up at the stage, the boy quietly vowed that one day he too would stand where the politician now stood, and speak for those who had no voice. （立志场景，为续写埋下抱负）

advancedExpressions.expression: we are privileged to have a distinguished politician as our guest speaker
advancedExpressions.example: We are privileged to have a distinguished politician as our guest speaker, whose insights into public service will surely inspire us all. （正式邀请，抬高来宾分量）

advancedExpressions.expression: a politician is judged not by ... but by ...
advancedExpressions.example: A politician is judged, in the end, not by the eloquence of his promises but by the honesty of his deeds. （否定表象、强调实质，对比句式）

sentenceUpgrade.original: Franklin was a scientist and a politician.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Franklin was a man of astonishing range — a scientist, a writer, an inventor and a politician — whose restless curiosity left its mark on almost every field he touched. （说明/记叙·人物介绍）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 破折号插入并列身份 + a man of astonishing range 概括性评价 + 定语从句(whose restless curiosity...)收束 + 抽象升华

sentenceUpgrade.original: A good politician helps people.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: A truly great politician measures his worth not by the office he holds but by the countless ordinary lives his decisions quietly improve. （议论文·价值论证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: truly great 加强 + measure one's worth by 抽象化 + not...but... 对比结构 + 定语从句(his decisions quietly improve)落到实处

original_sentence: Franklin had found lightning interesting for years, believing it was actually electricity.
readingExamples: Franklin had found lightning interesting for years, believing it was actually electricity.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a bright flash of light in the sky produced by natural electricity during a storm, usually followed by thunder
(2) n. the electrical discharge that causes this flash
(3) adj. (before noun) extremely quick or sudden
(4) v. (of the sky) to produce flashes of lightning

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 闪电般迅速的；突如其来的
uncommonMeanings.example: With lightning reflexes the goalkeeper flung himself sideways, and the ball that seemed certain to score smacked harmlessly into his gloves. （读后续写·体育竞技·反应迅捷）

posExamples.sentence: A jagged bolt of lightning split the black sky, and for one blinding instant the whole valley leapt into ghostly white, freezing the terrified sheep mid-flight across the field. （读后续写·暴风雨·环境渲染）
I am writing to remind every hiker that, should lightning strike during our mountain trip, you must stay away from tall trees and crouch low until the danger has passed. （应用文·安全提示/通知）
The dazzling flash of lightning that revealed Franklin's discovery reminds us that nature's most fearsome forces, once understood, can be harnessed to serve rather than harm mankind. （议论文·科学与自然）
Moving with lightning speed, the young rescuer dashed through the smoke, scooped up the crying child and was back on the street before the crowd could even draw breath. （读后续写·危难救援·动作）

wordForms.adjective: lightning (置于名词前作定语：闪电般的，如 lightning speed)
wordForms.other: 重点辨析：lightning /ˈlaɪtnɪŋ/ 闪电(名词) ≠ lightening /ˈlaɪtnɪŋ/ (动词 lighten 的现在分词，意为'使变亮/减轻')。前者无 e，后者有 e。另有 lightning-fast (adj. 极快的)

idioms.idiom: lightning never strikes twice (in the same place)
idioms.translation: 闪电不会两次击中同一处；同样的坏事不会重演
idioms.example: Try again — they say lightning never strikes twice, so surely fortune will smile on you this time. （读后续写·鼓励安慰）
The moment the bell rang, the boys shot out of the classroom like greased lightning, satchels bouncing on their backs. （读后续写·校园生活·画面）

collocations.translation: 觉得闪电有趣（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Franklin had found lightning interesting for years, believing it was actually electricity. （课文原句）

collocations.translation: 一道闪电（lightning 不可数，用 a flash/bolt of 表'一道'）
collocations.example: A sudden flash of lightning lit up the whole valley for one blinding instant. （读后续写·暴风雨）
The old shepherd warned us never to shelter under a lone tree, for a friend of his had once been struck by lightning there. （安全告诫）
When lightning struck the ancient oak, it burst into flame and toppled with a groan that echoed across the sleeping village. （读后续写·灾难场景）
All night the storm raged on, thunder and lightning tearing the sky apart while the children huddled together. （读后续写·暴风雨之夜）
News of the victory spread through the town at lightning speed, and within an hour the square was packed. （读后续写·消息传播）
Franklin's invention of the lightning rod protected countless buildings from the destructive power he had studied. （议论文·科学贡献）
Quick as lightning, she snatched the falling vase before it could shatter on the marble floor. （读后续写·瞬间反应）

collocations.translation: 一次闪电；（引申）突然袭击
collocations.example: A single lightning strike had set the dry hillside ablaze, and by nightfall the whole ridge was a wall of roaring fire. （读后续写·山火）
A sudden bolt of lightning lit up the deserted street, and in that flickering glare she glimpsed a figure standing perfectly still by the gate. （读后续写·悬疑氛围）

synonyms.example: A brilliant flash tore across the heavens, and thunder rolled after it like distant drums of war. （读后续写·环境描写）
synonyms.usage: 泛指任何突然而短暂的强光，不限于闪电；lightning 特指暴风雨中的自然放电现象

synonyms.example: A bolt from the storm-dark sky struck the church steeple, sending sparks showering into the rain. （读后续写·雷暴）
synonyms.usage: 常与 of lightning 连用或单独指‘一道闪电’，强调其笔直、猛烈；lightning 是整体现象的统称

advancedExpressions.expression: no sooner had the lightning flashed than ...
advancedExpressions.example: No sooner had the lightning flashed than a deafening crack of thunder shook the windows, and the frightened puppy dived under the sofa. （no sooner...than 倒装，制造紧张节奏，烘托暴风雨的骤然）

advancedExpressions.expression: in the event of lightning, be sure to ...
advancedExpressions.example: In the event of lightning, be sure to switch off electrical appliances and keep well clear of open water. （in the event of 正式条件表达，用于通知/须知类应用文）

advancedExpressions.expression: just as Franklin dared to reach for the lightning, so ...
advancedExpressions.example: Just as Franklin dared to reach for the lightning that others merely feared, so every generation must summon the courage to probe the unknown. （just as...so 类比结构，将历史事例升华为普遍论点）

sentenceUpgrade.original: There was a lot of lightning in the storm.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Bolt after bolt of lightning ripped through the heaving clouds, each flash carving the drenched landscape into brief, trembling silver before darkness swallowed it whole again. （读后续写·暴风雨渲染）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Bolt after bolt 重复叠加强化视觉冲击 + carving...into silver 动词化比喻 + before darkness swallowed it 拟人收束，形成明暗交替的画面节奏

sentenceUpgrade.original: Franklin studied lightning bravely.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It was Franklin's fearless resolve to unravel the mystery of lightning — a force that had terrified humankind for millennia — that laid the very foundation of our modern understanding of electricity. （议论文·强调句）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It was...that 强调句突出人物精神 + 破折号插入语补充背景 + unravel the mystery/laid the foundation 正式书面搭配

classPractice.question: Franklin had found ____ (lightning) interesting for years, believing it was actually electricity.
classPractice.note: 课文原句；lightning 闪电为不可数名词，前不加冠词，也不加 s

classPractice.question: 用 a flash of / a piece of 填空：Suddenly ____ lightning tore across the black sky, and thunder followed at once.
classPractice.note: lightning 不可数，表'一道闪电'用 a flash/bolt of lightning，不用 a lightning

classPractice.question: 用 lightning / lightening 填空：As the storm gathered, a bolt of ____ split the sky, while in the east the horizon was slowly ____.
classPractice.note: lightning 闪电(名词，无 e)；lightening 变亮(lighten 的现在分词，有 e)，形近词高频考点

original_sentence: Franklin had found lightning interesting for years, believing it was actually electricity.
readingExamples: Franklin had found lightning interesting for years, believing it was actually electricity.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a form of energy carried through wires and used to provide light, heat, and power, or to run machines
(2) n. the flow of electric charge, especially as used to supply power
(3) n. a feeling of great excitement, tension, or emotion between people or in a place

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （人与人之间或场合中的）激动情绪，紧张兴奋的气氛
uncommonMeanings.example: As the two rivals finally met each other's eyes across the ring, a current of electricity ran through the silent crowd, and no one dared even to breathe. （读后续写·对决氛围·情绪张力）

posExamples.sentence: When the flickering lamp finally steadied and warm electricity flooded the cottage, the old couple clasped hands and gazed at the glowing bulb as though it were a small, miraculous sun. （读后续写·山村通电·喜悦）
I am writing to appeal to every resident to save electricity by switching off idle lights and unplugging chargers, so that together we may build a greener, more responsible community. （应用文·倡议书）

That we can generate electricity from sunlight and wind rather than burning coal proves beyond doubt that human ingenuity, once awakened, can reconcile progress with the health of our planet. （议论文·清洁能源）
Franklin's daring kite experiment first revealed that lightning and electricity are one and the same, a discovery that would one day illuminate the whole world. （读后续写/说明·科学史）

wordForms.noun: electricity (电，电能，不可数) / electrician (电工) / electron (电子)
wordForms.other: 三个形容词辨析：electric 用电的、带电的(具体电器/效果)，如 an electric car / electric shock；electrical 与电有关的、电气的(领域/系统)，如 electrical engineering / an electrical fault；electronic 电子的(含芯片元件)，如 electronic devices / an electronic dictionary

collocations.translation: 闪电其实就是电（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Franklin had found lightning interesting for years, believing it was actually electricity. （课文原句）
The new dam will generate enough electricity to light up a dozen surrounding villages. （议论文/应用文·能源建设）
By reminding one another to save electricity, we can each play a small part in protecting the environment. （应用文·倡议）
For three long days the storm cut off the electricity supply, and the whole town rediscovered the comfort of candlelight. （读后续写·停电经历）
The teacher showed us how a copper wire conducts electricity far more readily than a strand of dry cotton. （说明文·实验课）
A sudden current of electricity shot up his arm, and he leapt back from the exposed wire with a startled cry. （读后续写·意外·动作反应）
These sleek new buses run entirely on electricity, gliding through the streets without a single puff of smoke. （议论文·绿色出行）
Their careful habits soon showed on the electricity bill, which had shrunk to barely half of what it once was. （应用文·家庭节能）
The moment the engineers restored the electricity, cheers rang out from every window along the flooded street. （读后续写·灾后重建）

synonyms.example: When the power came back on, the hospital's silent corridors suddenly hummed back to life. （读后续写·恢复供电）
synonyms.usage: 口语和日常中常用 power 指‘电力供应’（如 power cut 停电），比 electricity 更宽泛，也可指其他动力；electricity 更强调‘电’这种能量本身

synonyms.example: Scientists are racing to capture clean energy from the sun before fossil fuels run dry. （议论文·可持续发展）
synonyms.usage: 泛指一切形式的能量（热能、动能、太阳能等），概念最广；electricity 是 energy 的一种具体形式

synonyms.example: A faint current flickered through the frayed wire, just enough to make the tiny bulb glow. （说明文·电路）
synonyms.usage: 特指‘电流’这一物理量，强调电荷的流动；electricity 指作为整体的电这种现象或能源

advancedExpressions.expression: the air was charged with electricity
advancedExpressions.example: The air in the crowded hall was charged with electricity as the final name was about to be read out, and a hundred hearts pounded as one. （借 electricity 的‘紧张气氛’义营造悬念高潮）

advancedExpressions.expression: let us make it a habit to save electricity by ...
advancedExpressions.example: Let us make it a habit to save electricity by pulling the curtains for natural light and switching to energy-saving bulbs. （let us...by 呼吁+具体做法，标准倡议书句式）

advancedExpressions.expression: generating electricity from ... is not merely ..., but ...
advancedExpressions.example: Generating electricity from renewable sources is not merely a technological choice but a moral commitment to the generations yet to come. （not merely...but 递进，将技术问题上升到道德高度）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The village finally had electricity.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: When electricity at last reached the remote mountain village, the children pressed their faces to the windows, marvelling at how a single glowing bulb could turn night into a warm and welcoming day. （读后续写·山村通电）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: When...at last 时间状语突出等待之久 + pressed their faces/marvelling 细节动作与心理 + turn night into day 对比升华意义

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should use less electricity to protect the environment.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is high time that each of us cut down on electricity consumption, for every kilowatt saved is a small yet genuine gift to the fragile planet we all call home. （议论文·呼吁）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is high time that + 过去式虚拟语气增强紧迫感 + every...is a gift 隐喻升华 + fragile planet we call home 情感共鸣

classPractice.question: Franklin had found lightning interesting for years, believing it was actually ____ (electric).
classPractice.note: 课文原句；此处作名词'电'，用 electricity，而非形容词 electric

classPractice.question: 用 electric / electrical / electronic 填空：The fire was caused by an ____ fault in the old wiring, not by the new ____ car parked in the garage.
classPractice.note: electrical fault 电气故障(系统层面)；electric car 电动车(用电驱动)；electronic 则指含芯片的电子产品

classPractice.question: 这座大坝每年能发出足够的电供整个城市使用。The dam can ____ enough ____ (电) for the whole city every year.
classPractice.note: generate electricity 发电，固定搭配；electricity 不可数名词，前不加冠词、不加 s

original_sentence: He designed an experiment to prove his theory.
readingExamples: He designed an experiment to prove his theory.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a formal set of ideas intended to explain why something happens or exists, based on principles and evidence
(2) n. an idea or opinion that someone thinks is true but that has not yet been proved
(3) n. the general principles or ideas that form the basis of a subject, as opposed to its practice
(4) n. (in theory) used to say that something should be true or possible but may not actually be so

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （个人的）看法，推测，臆想（未经证实）
uncommonMeanings.example: "My theory," she whispered, narrowing her eyes at the muddy footprints, "is that our visitor came in through the garden long before midnight." （读后续写·侦探推理·个人推测）

posExamples.sentence: Late into the night the young inventor scribbled equations by candlelight, convinced that a single bold theory could unlock a door that had baffled scholars for centuries. （读后续写·科学探索·执着）
In my speech I would like to argue that no theory, however elegant, deserves our trust until it has withstood the honest test of experiment. （应用文·演讲稿）
A sound theory is not the enemy of practice but its guiding star, for it shows us not only what works but, more importantly, why it works. （议论文·理论与实践）
Franklin refused to accept the popular theory on faith alone; instead, he designed a daring experiment to prove his theory that lightning was electricity. （读后续写/说明·科学史）

wordForms.noun: theory (理论，学说) / theorist (理论家) / theorem (定理)
wordForms.other: 短语 in theory (理论上) 常与 in practice (实际上) 对照使用；辨析近义：theory(较成熟的解释体系) > hypothesis(待验证的假说) > assumption(想当然的假定)

idioms.translation: 理论上（往往与实际相反）
idioms.example: In theory the plan was flawless; in practice, however, a single gust of wind was enough to send it crashing to the ground. （议论文/读后续写·理论与现实对比）

collocations.phrase: come up with / put forward / propose a theory
collocations.example: After years of observation, Darwin finally put forward a theory that would reshape the whole of biology. （课件·提出一个理论）

collocations.translation: 【课件】……理论（如 the theory of evolution / relativity）
collocations.example: Einstein's theory of relativity overturned the way we understand time and space. （课件·the theory of sth）

collocations.translation: 【课件】理论上讲，按理说（常与 in practice 对照）
collocations.example: In theory the plan should work perfectly, though no one has yet tried it in practice. （课件·in theory 理论上讲）
A good engineer must be able to put theory into practice, turning equations on paper into machines that truly run. （课件·将理论付诸实践）

collocations.translation: 证明某人的理论（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: He designed an experiment to prove his theory. （课文原句）
Darwin spent decades gathering evidence before he dared publish the theory of evolution. （议论文·科学史）
He designed an ingenious experiment to prove his theory, staking his reputation on a result he could not yet see. （读后续写·科研）
When the young scholar put forward his bold new theory, the hall fell silent, uncertain whether to applaud or protest. （读后续写·学术场景）
Over decades of patient observation, she developed a theory that would eventually transform the way we see the stars. （议论文·科学成就）
Every new fossil unearthed that summer seemed to support the theory the professor had defended for thirty lonely years. （读后续写·坚持）
True mastery is born only where theory and practice meet, each correcting and enriching the other. （议论文·成才之道）
It takes rigorous evidence, not a sensational conspiracy theory, to earn the title of genuine scientific knowledge. （议论文·科学素养）
His humble experiment quietly overturned a theory that had gone unquestioned for a thousand years. （读后续写·科学突破）
In theory everyone agreed the rule was fair; in practice, few were willing to obey it. （议论文·理想与现实）

collocations.translation: 理论上（往往与实际相反）
collocations.example: In theory the plan was flawless; in practice, a single gust of wind sent it crashing down. （议论文·理论与现实）

synonyms.translation: 【课件】理论上的（adj.）/ 理论上，从理论上讲（adv.）
synonyms.example: Theoretically the machine could run forever, yet in practice friction wears it down within days. （课件·theory→theoretical adj.→theoretically adv. 词族拓展）
synonyms.usage: 【课件】theory 的词族：theoretical (adj. 理论上的)、theoretically (adv. 理论上讲，从理论上说)；theoretically 常与 in practice/actually 对照，等同于 in theory

synonyms.example: Before touching the equipment, the students first wrote down a clear hypothesis to guide their experiment. （说明文·实验步骤）
synonyms.usage: 指尚待验证的'假设/初步猜想'，比 theory 更初步、更暂定；theory 通常已有较多证据支撑，是较成熟的解释体系

synonyms.example: The whole machine, however complex, rested on a single elegant principle of balance. （说明文·科学原理）
synonyms.usage: 指普遍成立的'基本原理/规律'，强调其确定性和奠基性；theory 是对现象的解释框架，可能被修正或推翻

synonyms.example: His entire argument collapsed the moment that one shaky assumption was proved false. （议论文·逻辑漏洞）
synonyms.usage: 指未经证明就当作前提的'假定'，含'想当然'的意味；theory 则是有意识、成体系的解释

advancedExpressions.expression: however wild the theory seemed, sb. was determined to ...
advancedExpressions.example: However wild the theory seemed to his mocking colleagues, the young man was determined to put it to the test, come what may. （however + 形容词 让步 + come what may 决心表达，刻画探索者的执着）

advancedExpressions.expression: let us not mistake a mere theory for established truth
advancedExpressions.example: Let us not mistake a mere theory for established truth; only tireless experiment can turn a bold guess into knowledge we may safely rely on. （let us not... 演讲呼告句式，警示听众理性求证）

advancedExpressions.expression: a theory is worth little unless it can be put into practice
advancedExpressions.example: A theory, however dazzling on paper, is worth little unless it can be put into practice and made to serve real human needs. （unless 条件让步 + however 插入，强调理论必须落地）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He wanted to prove his theory was right.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Driven by an unshakeable faith in his own theory, he braved the raging storm, kite in hand, resolved to wrest the truth from the very heavens themselves. （读后续写·科学探索）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Driven by...状语前置突出动机 + braved the storm/kite in hand 动作与细节 + wrest the truth from the heavens 比喻升华，呼应富兰克林情境

sentenceUpgrade.original: Theory is not useful without practice.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It must be acknowledged that even the most brilliant theory remains an empty vessel until practice fills it with life, for knowledge untested is knowledge unearned. （议论文·正式论证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It must be acknowledged that 让步引入 + empty vessel...fills it with life 隐喻 + knowledge untested is knowledge unearned 对称警句收束

original_sentence: He worked out that by flying a kite during a thunderstorm, electricity could go through the wet kite line down to the earth.
readingExamples: He worked out that by flying a kite during a thunderstorm, electricity could go through the wet kite line down to the earth.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a storm with thunder and lightning, and usually heavy rain
(2) n. a period of violent weather marked by thunder, lightning, and often strong winds

posExamples.sentence: A violent thunderstorm swept in from the sea that evening, hurling rain against the windows and drowning the frightened children's voices beneath its relentless roar. （读后续写·暴风雨·环境渲染）
I am writing to warn all campers that a severe thunderstorm is forecast for Saturday night, so please pack your tents securely and avoid pitching them near tall trees. （应用文·通知/提醒）
Franklin's willingness to fly a kite in the heart of a thunderstorm shows that true progress often demands the courage to step, quite literally, into the storm. （议论文·勇气与探索）
When the thunderstorm finally spent its fury and the first pale sunlight crept over the drenched hills, the whole village emerged, blinking, into a world washed startlingly clean. （读后续写·风雨过后·希望）

wordForms.other: 【构词法·合成词】thunderstorm = thunder(雷) + storm(暴风雨)，两个名词合成为“雷暴”；同类合成：thundercloud (n. 雷云)、thunderbolt (n. 霹雳)、rainstorm (n. 暴雨)、snowstorm (n. 暴风雪)

collocations.phrase: during a thunderstorm（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: He worked out that by flying a kite during a thunderstorm, electricity could go through the wet kite line down to the earth. （课文原句）
A severe thunderstorm battered the coast all night, tearing branches from the trees and flooding the narrow lanes. （读后续写·灾害）
Just as they reached the summit, a thunderstorm broke without warning, and rain came lashing down in cold grey sheets. （读后续写·登山遇险）
Caught in a sudden thunderstorm far from shelter, the hikers huddled together beneath a low rock and waited, soaked and shivering. （读后续写·户外·困境）

collocations.translation: 预报有雷暴/雷暴即将来临
collocations.example: Dark clouds massed on the horizon, and everyone sensed that a thunderstorm was brewing over the restless sea. （读后续写·暴风雨前）
Only when the thunderstorm had at last passed did the birds venture back into the dripping, sunlit branches. （读后续写·雨过天晴）
They dashed into an abandoned barn to shelter from the thunderstorm, hearts still hammering from the last blinding flash. （读后续写·避雨）

synonyms.example: The fishing boats raced for the harbour as the storm closed in, its black clouds swallowing the last of the daylight. （读后续写·海上风暴）
synonyms.usage: 泛指各种猛烈天气（含雪暴、沙暴等），范围最广；thunderstorm 特指伴有雷电的暴风雨

synonyms.translation: 大风暴，狂风暴雨（文学用语）
synonyms.example: The old sailor spoke of a tempest so wild it had once torn the very sails from the mast. （读后续写·文学叙事）
synonyms.usage: 多见于文学或正式语体，感情色彩强烈、带戏剧性；thunderstorm 是中性、日常的气象名词

synonyms.example: A sudden downpour left them drenched to the skin within seconds, laughing helplessly under the streaming sky. （读后续写·骤雨）
synonyms.usage: 只强调‘大雨倾泻’，不必有雷电；thunderstorm 侧重雷电交加的整体天气现象

advancedExpressions.expression: as the thunderstorm raged, sb. ...
advancedExpressions.example: As the thunderstorm raged outside, tearing at the shutters like an angry beast, the family gathered round the single flickering candle and told stories to keep their fear at bay. （as 时间状语 + like an angry beast 拟物比喻，以外境衬内心）

advancedExpressions.expression: in case a thunderstorm should occur, please ...
advancedExpressions.example: In case a thunderstorm should occur during the outing, please move indoors at once and stay away from windows and metal fences. （in case + should 虚拟条件，用于须知/通知的稳妥提醒）

advancedExpressions.expression: just as a thunderstorm clears the air, so ...
advancedExpressions.example: Just as a thunderstorm clears the stifling air and leaves the world fresher than before, so hardship, painful though it is, often purifies and strengthens the human spirit. （just as...so 类比，将天气现象升华为人生哲理）

sentenceUpgrade.original: There was a big thunderstorm and everyone was scared.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: A ferocious thunderstorm descended upon the town without mercy, and as lightning split the heavens and thunder shook the very floorboards, even the bravest among them felt their courage waver. （读后续写·暴风雨·群体反应）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: descended upon...without mercy 拟人+夸张 + split the heavens/shook the floorboards 平行动作 + even the bravest...waver 以退为进写恐惧

sentenceUpgrade.original: Franklin flew a kite in a thunderstorm to do his experiment.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Undaunted by the fury of the thunderstorm, Franklin sent his fragile kite soaring into the boiling clouds, staking his life on the conviction that lightning and electricity were, in truth, one and the same. （议论文/读后续写·科学勇气）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Undaunted by 状语突出无畏 + sent...soaring into the boiling clouds 动态画面 + staking his life on the conviction 强调信念的分量

classPractice.question: He worked out that by flying a kite during a ____ (thunder), electricity could go through the wet kite line down to the earth.
classPractice.note: 回归课文原句；thunder + storm 合成名词，可数，此处需名词形式

classPractice.question: 他们在离庇护所很远的地方遭遇了一场突如其来的雷暴。They ____ ____ ____ a sudden thunderstorm far from any shelter.
classPractice.note: be caught in a thunderstorm “遭遇雷暴”，介词用 in，注意主谓一致用过去时

classPractice.answer: Dark clouds gathered overhead, and everyone sensed that a thunderstorm was brewing / coming. / Dark clouds massed overhead, and everyone felt a thunderstorm was approaching.

original_sentence: Franklin held a silk ribbon tied to the end of it.
readingExamples: Franklin held a silk ribbon tied to the end of it.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a narrow strip of fabric used for tying things or as a decoration, especially in the hair or on a gift
(2) n. a narrow strip of material awarded as a prize or worn to show support for a cause
(3) n. a long, narrow strip of anything, such as ink-soaked tape in a printer or a winding road or river
(4) v. to decorate or tie with ribbons

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （细长的）带状物；蜿蜒的一条（路、河、光等）
uncommonMeanings.example: From the mountaintop the highway lay far below them, a thin silver ribbon unwinding lazily through the sleeping valley. （读后续写·登高远眺·景物描写）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 碎条，破布条（cut/tear ... to ribbons 撕成碎片）
uncommonMeanings.example: The gale had torn the ship's proud sails to ribbons, and the crew clung grimly to the ropes as the deck heaved beneath them. （读后续写·海上遇险·紧张）

posExamples.sentence: She tied a bright red ribbon in her little sister's hair, tucking a stray curl behind her ear, and the child beamed up at her as if crowned a princess. （读后续写·姐妹亲情·细节）
On behalf of the organizing committee, I warmly invite you to the opening ceremony, where our headmaster will cut the ribbon to mark the launch of the new library. （应用文·邀请信）
The blue ribbon pinned to his chest was, in the end, far less precious than the discipline and perseverance the long months of training had quietly forged in him. （议论文·过程重于奖赏）
Franklin held a silk ribbon tied to the end of the kite line, keeping his hand safely dry so that the deadly current could not pass through his body. （说明文·实验细节）

wordForms.other: ribbon-shaped (adj. 带状的)

idioms.translation: 把某物撕成碎片；（喻）狠狠批驳、彻底击垮
idioms.example: The critics tore his first play to ribbons, yet the young writer swallowed his tears and vowed to prove them wrong. （读后续写·挫折与坚持）

collocations.phrase: a silk ribbon（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Franklin held a silk ribbon tied to the end of it. （课文原句）

collocations.phrase: a ribbon of light / road / river
collocations.example: Far ahead, a ribbon of moonlight lay across the dark water, as though pointing the lost sailors gently home. （读后续写·景物·希望）

synonyms.example: A slender band of gold gleamed at her wrist, catching the candlelight with every graceful gesture. （读后续写·人物描写）
synonyms.usage: 指较宽或较硬的‘带、箍、环’，常为环状；ribbon 通常是柔软、狭长、可打结的织带

synonyms.example: He tore a strip of cloth from his own shirt to bind the injured boy's bleeding hand. （读后续写·救助·动作）
synonyms.usage: 泛指从整体上撕/切下的‘一条’材料，中性且不具装饰义；ribbon 多为成品织带，常带装饰或纪念意味

synonyms.example: Colourful streamers fluttered from every window as the victory parade wound through the cheering streets. （读后续写·庆祝场面）
synonyms.usage: 特指节庆时悬挂、飘扬的‘长彩带’，强调飘动的装饰效果；ribbon 更小巧，多用于系扎或佩戴

advancedExpressions.expression: like a ribbon of silver/silk, the ... wound through ...

advancedExpressions.expression: we would be honoured if you could cut the ribbon at ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: She put a ribbon in her hair.

sentenceUpgrade.techniques: With trembling fingers 状语前置传情 + 破折号插入语勾连回忆 + as though...not so alone 心理描写升华物件的情感重量

sentenceUpgrade.original: The guest cut the ribbon and the shop opened.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: As the honoured guest gently drew the scissors together and the crimson ribbon fluttered to the ground, a wave of applause swept through the crowd, and years of hard work finally blossomed into this shining moment. （读后续写/应用文·开幕式）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: As 时间状语引导同步动作 + fluttered to the ground 细节特写 + years of hard work blossomed into 隐喻，将剪彩瞬间升华为奋斗成果

original_sentence: Then he attached a metal key where the ribbon and kite line joined.

idioms.translation: 把油门踩到底；全力以赴

collocations.phrase: a metal key（课文原句词块）

collocations.translation: 金属般的声音/味道/光泽

translation: 很成功；引人注目，有强烈影响

(2) n. a person or thing that is much better than or clearly distinguished from the others in a group
(3) adj. (of a quality or feature) that is easy to notice because it is remarkable or unusual

posExamples.sentence: Of all the acts that evening, hers was the standout performance — the instant her bow touched the strings, the restless hall fell utterly still, spellbound by a talent no one had expected from so quiet a girl. （读后续写·才艺·惊艳全场）
Among the many exhibits at the fair, the clear standout was a solar-powered model car built by a group of first-year students working late into the night. （应用文·活动报道）
What makes a truly standout leader is not the loudest voice in the room, but the rare ability to listen, to empathise, and to lift others up. （议论文·领导力）
In a class of gifted writers, she remained the standout, not because she wrote the most, but because every word she chose seemed to breathe. （读后续写·出类拔萃）

Among dozens of entries, her hand-painted poster was the clear standout, drawing admiring crowds all afternoon. （应用文·比赛报道）

synonyms.example: Her outstanding dedication to the volunteer team inspired everyone around her to give a little more. （应用文·表彰）
synonyms.usage: outstanding 是最通用的正式褒义词,书面口语皆宜;standout 语气更鲜明,强调'在一群人/物中一眼就脱颖而出',常修饰 performance/moment/feature

synonyms.example: The debate over nuclear power has divided scientists and citizens alike for decades. （议论文·争议）
synonyms.usage: nuclear 是现代科技和政治语境中的常用词(nuclear power/weapon/energy),范围更广更正式;atomic 更传统,常见于 atomic bomb 等固定历史表达,二者在'核能/核武'义上常互换

synonyms.example: Advances in molecular biology have opened astonishing new frontiers in medicine. （议论文·科技进步）
synonyms.usage: molecular 指分子层面,层级比 atomic(原子层面)高一级;二者都用于科学语境,但描述对象的尺度不同,不可混用

advancedExpressions.expression: haunted by the ... of the atomic ..., sb devoted the rest of his life to ...
advancedExpressions.example: Haunted by the devastation the atomic bomb had wrought, he devoted the rest of his life to a single cause — ensuring that such a horror would never again be unleashed upon the world. （分词状语+破折号,续写人物救赎弧光）

advancedExpressions.expression: understanding atomic energy is the first step towards ...
advancedExpressions.example: Understanding atomic energy is the first step towards using it responsibly; I therefore urge every student to attend this eye-opening lecture. （倡议信论点+呼吁）

advancedExpressions.expression: the atomic age reminds us that ... must go hand in hand with ...
advancedExpressions.example: The atomic age reminds us that scientific brilliance must go hand in hand with moral responsibility, lest our greatest discoveries become our undoing. （议论文·科技与道德辩证）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He felt sorry that he had helped make the atomic bomb.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Not a day passed without the weight of what he had done pressing upon his heart; having helped bring the atomic bomb into being, he now carried its shadow like an invisible chain he could never quite set down. （读后续写·分词状语+隐喻）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Not a day passed without... 强调持续的煎熬 + having helped... 完成式分词状语交代因果 + shadow/invisible chain 双重隐喻具象化愧疚

sentenceUpgrade.original: Atomic energy can be good or bad.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Atomic energy is a double-edged sword: in the hands of the wise it can illuminate the darkest corners of the earth, yet in the hands of the reckless it can plunge civilisation itself into ruin. （议论文·比喻+对比句式）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: double-edged sword 隐喻立论 + 冒号引出双面论证 + in the hands of... 对称结构 + illuminate 与 plunge into ruin 强烈对比升华主题

classPractice.answer: Used wisely, atomic energy can light millions of homes. / If it is used properly, atomic / nuclear energy can light up thousands of households.

translation: n. 炸弹；核武器 | vt. 轰炸
original_sentence: But then during the war I worked on the atomic bomb.
readingExamples: But then during the war I worked on the atomic bomb.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a weapon made of material that will explode, used to destroy people, buildings or other targets
(2) vt. to attack a place with bombs, especially by dropping them from an aircraft
(3) n. (informal, British English) a large amount of money
(4) vi. (informal) to fail completely, especially in public

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （口语）彻底失败；（表演、计划等）砸锅
uncommonMeanings.example: The comedian's new show bombed on opening night; standing behind the curtain, he listened to the thin, scattered applause and felt his stomach knot with humiliation. （读后续写·失败挫折·舞台上的窘迫）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （英式口语）一大笔钱
uncommonMeanings.example: That vintage watch on his wrist must have cost a bomb, yet he wore it as carelessly as if it were a plastic toy. （读后续写·人物刻画·财富与随性）

posExamples.sentence: The moment the air-raid siren wailed, the old man clutched his granddaughter and dived under the table, his mind flooded with memories of the night a bomb had flattened his childhood home. （读后续写·战争创伤·瞬间恐惧）

On behalf of our history club, I am writing to invite you to an exhibition commemorating the cities that were bombed during the war, so that the younger generation may cherish the peace we now enjoy. （应用文·邀请信）

As long as nations continue to stockpile nuclear bombs, the shadow of mutual destruction will hang over humanity, reminding us that true security lies not in weapons but in trust and cooperation. （议论文·和平主题）

idioms.translation: （英式口语）大获成功，非常受欢迎
idioms.example: Her heartfelt speech went down a bomb with the audience, and the applause thundered through the hall long after she had left the stage. （读后续写·演讲成功）

idioms.translation: 突然宣布令人震惊的消息
idioms.example: Just as the family sat down to dinner, Father dropped a bombshell: he had quit the job he had held for twenty years. （读后续写·家庭冲突·意外消息）

collocations.translation: 原子弹（课文原句：工作于原子弹研制）
collocations.example: But then during the war I worked on the atomic bomb. （课文原句）

collocations.translation: 炸弹爆炸（go off = explode，高频）
collocations.example: A bomb went off near the market, and panic swept through the crowd. （读后续写·突发事件）

collocations.translation: 票房惨败的影片（熟词僻义：bomb = 惨败之作）
collocations.example: Despite its huge budget, the film turned out to be a box-office bomb. （议论文·影视产业）
The scientist spent his final years campaigning against the very atomic bomb his research had helped to create. （议论文·科学与责任）
Reports that terrorists had planted a bomb in the station threw the whole city into panic. （读后续写·危机时刻）
A bomb went off in the distance, and the ground shuddered beneath their feet like a wounded animal. （读后续写·战场环境描写）
With trembling but steady hands, the young officer defused the bomb seconds before the timer reached zero. （读后续写·英雄壮举·紧张时刻）
For weeks, enemy planes dropped bombs on the harbour, reducing the once-bustling port to smoking ruins. （读后续写·战争废墟）

collocations.phrase: a bomb attack / a bombing raid
collocations.example: The museum was rebuilt on the exact spot where a bombing raid had destroyed it decades earlier. （读后续写·重建与希望）
A bomb scare forced the whole school to evacuate onto the playground in the pouring rain. （读后续写·突发事件）
Repairing the flooded library would cost a bomb, yet the headmaster insisted that no child should lose access to books. （应用文·校园话题）

synonyms.example: Sniffer dogs were trained to detect even the faintest trace of explosives hidden in the luggage. （应用文·安全说明）
synonyms.usage: 泛指爆炸性物质（TNT、炸药等），概念比 bomb 更广；bomb 特指制成的、可投放或引爆的完整武器装置。

synonyms.example: Shells screamed overhead as the soldiers pressed themselves flat against the muddy trench wall. （读后续写·战场描写）
synonyms.usage: 指由火炮发射的炮弹，强调'发射'而非'投放/安放'；描写地面炮战时用 shell，描写空袭或恐怖袭击时用 bomb。

advancedExpressions.expression: the atomic bomb / a bomb goes off / defuse a bomb / drop bombs on / cost a bomb
advancedExpressions.example: During the war he worked on the atomic bomb; years later, hearing a bomb go off on the news still made his hands shake. （一网打尽 bomb 的名词与动词搭配）

advancedExpressions.expression: bomb (n./v.) → bomber (轰炸机/投弹者) → bombing (轰炸) → bombardment (炮击) → bombshell (爆炸性消息)
advancedExpressions.example: The bomber dropped its load, and the bombing left the town a ruin; but the real bombshell came later, when the pilot's diary was published. （名词后缀 -er/-ing/-ment 派生词族）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·(表演/计划)彻底失败
advancedExpressions.expression: bomb / flop / fall flat / be a fiasco / go down like a lead balloon
advancedExpressions.example: The much-hyped launch bombed / flopped / fell flat, and investors quietly walked away. （可替换的"惨败"表达，用于影视、演出、计划）

advancedExpressions.expression: no sooner had the bomb ... than ...
advancedExpressions.example: No sooner had the bomb exploded than a suffocating cloud of dust swallowed the street, muffling every scream into an eerie silence. （no sooner...than 倒装 + 环境窒息感，制造混乱紧张氛围）

advancedExpressions.expression: lest we forget the price paid ...
advancedExpressions.example: We hold this memorial not to reopen old wounds but lest we forget the price paid by those who perished when the bombs fell. （lest 引导目的状语，庄重悼念语气）

advancedExpressions.expression: the same knowledge that ... can also ...
advancedExpressions.example: The same knowledge that split the atom to light our cities can also be forged into a bomb capable of erasing them — proof that science without conscience is a blade without a hilt. （对比结构 + 比喻，论证科技的双刃性）

sentenceUpgrade.original: A bomb fell and destroyed the house.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: In a heartbeat, a bomb tore through the roof, and the house that had sheltered three generations collapsed into a heap of splintered wood and swirling ash. （读后续写·瞬间毁灭）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 时间状语 In a heartbeat 强化突发性 + tore through 动词升级 + 定语从句 that had sheltered three generations 注入情感重量 + 具象化结尾（splintered wood and swirling ash）

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should not make more nuclear bombs.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is my firm conviction that, rather than pouring precious resources into building ever more nuclear bombs, nations should redirect that ingenuity towards curing disease and healing our planet. （议论文·和平立场）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is my firm conviction that 正式主句 + rather than 对比让步 + ever more 强调升级 + 三宾语平行（curing disease, healing our planet）收束

classPractice.question: But then during the war I worked on ____ ____ ____ (原子弹).

classPractice.note: 熟词僻义：a box-office bomb = 票房惨败之作；语境"barely a tenth"锁定失败义。

translation: n. 罪恶，罪行；害处，坏处 | adj. 恶毒的；有害的；恶魔的
original_sentence: I had to ask myself, “Is there some evil involved in science?”
readingExamples: I had to ask myself, “Is there some evil involved in science?”
definitionEn:
(1) adj. morally wrong or bad; wicked and cruel
(2) adj. harmful or intending to harm; causing serious trouble
(3) n. a force or the personification of a force that is thought to bring about wickedness or misfortune
(4) n. something that is very bad and harmful, especially something that causes suffering in society

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 极其难闻的；令人厌恶的（指气味、天气等）
uncommonMeanings.example: An evil smell drifted from the abandoned kitchen, and she pressed a handkerchief to her nose before daring to step inside. （读后续写·探险场景·感官描写）

posExamples.sentence: There was something evil in the way the stranger smiled — a coldness in his eyes that made her spine tingle and her instinct scream at her to run. （读后续写·悬疑·人物危险感）
I firmly believe that indifference is a greater evil than open hostility, for it lets injustice grow unchecked while good people look the other way. （议论文·社会道德）
On behalf of the student union, I call on every classmate to speak out against the evil of bullying, so that our campus may become a place where kindness, not fear, prevails. （应用文·倡议书）

idioms.example: Cancelling the outdoor concert was the lesser of two evils; a soaked audience would have been far worse than a disappointed one. （议论文·抉择论证）

idioms.translation: 不可避免的祸害；必要之恶
idioms.example: Many students regard examinations as a necessary evil — stressful, yet indispensable for measuring how far we have truly come. （议论文·教育话题）
The old proverb warns that the love of money is the root of all evil, a truth the greedy merchant learned too late. （读后续写·道德寓言）

idioms.translation: 不说 / 不看坏事（三不猴之说）
idioms.example: By choosing to see no evil in his friend's cheating, he became, in a sense, an accomplice to it. （议论文·道德责任）

collocations.translation: 【课件】善与恶的斗争（good and evil 善与恶）
collocations.example: The novel is really a struggle with good and evil fought out within one man's heart. （课件搭配·善恶主题）
He who does evil to others will, sooner or later, have that evil returned upon himself. （课件搭配·因果报应）
The teacher warned us again and again about the evils of putting off today's work until tomorrow. （课件搭配·社会/习惯弊病）

collocations.translation: 【课件】……的负面影响（evil 作形容词）
collocations.example: Scientists have long studied the evil effects of long-term stress on the human heart. （课件搭配·evil adj. 有害的）

collocations.translation: 科学中掺杂的某种恶（课文原句）
collocations.example: I had to ask myself, "Is there some evil involved in science?" （课文原句）
The novel explores the eternal struggle between good and evil within every human heart. （议论文·文学主题）

collocations.phrase: the lesser evil / the lesser of two evils
collocations.translation: 较小的祸害；两害相权取其轻
collocations.example: Cancelling the trip was the lesser evil, for a drenched, exhausted class would have been far worse. （议论文·抉择论证）
No amount of charity, he realised, could ever wash away the evil deeds of his youth. （读后续写·忏悔救赎）
In every fairy tale, courage and love ultimately triumph over the forces of evil. （读后续写·童话结局）
The villagers lit lanterns all night, believing the light would keep evil spirits away. （读后续写·民俗场景）
To resist evil takes not only courage but also the humble willingness to admit one's own capacity for it. （议论文·人性论证）
Poverty, ignorance and injustice are the social evils that education, above all, is meant to cure. （议论文·教育价值）
He shot her an evil grin that made the hair on the back of her neck stand up. （读后续写·反派刻画）

synonyms.example: The wicked stepmother locked the girl in the attic and pocketed the key with a satisfied smile. （读后续写·童话反派）
synonyms.usage: 语气比 evil 略轻，常带故事化/口语色彩，多形容人的居心或行为；evil 更庄重、更绝对，可指抽象的'恶'本身。

synonyms.example: A vicious rumour spread through the school, and by lunchtime the innocent boy could hardly lift his head. （读后续写·校园伤害）
synonyms.usage: 强调残忍、攻击性和造成的实际伤害（凶狠的攻击、恶毒的谣言）；evil 强调道德本质上的邪恶。

synonyms.example: There was a sinister silence in the empty corridor, as if the walls themselves were holding their breath. （读后续写·悬疑氛围）
synonyms.usage: 侧重'令人不安、预示不祥'的暗示性氛围，未必已作恶；evil 是明确的道德判断。

advancedExpressions.expression: good and evil / the forces of evil / social evils / the lesser of two evils / a necessary evil
advancedExpressions.example: Weighing good and evil, she chose the lesser of two evils, telling herself that some suffering is a necessary evil on the road to justice. （名词义与形容词义常用组合一次记牢）

advancedExpressions.expression: evil / wicked / vicious / sinister / villainous
advancedExpressions.example: There was something evil / wicked / sinister about the way he smiled. （功能：形容人或氛围"邪恶、令人不安"，可据语气强弱替换）

advancedExpressions.expression: evil (n./adj.) → evilly (adv. 邪恶地) → evildoer (n. 作恶者)
advancedExpressions.example: He grinned evilly, the very picture of an evildoer who fears no punishment. （-ly 构副词，-doer 构"做……的人"）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·there be + something + adj. + about
advancedExpressions.expression: there was something evil about ...
advancedExpressions.example: There was something evil about the silence of that house. （something 后置形容词 evil；about 引出"关于……之处"）

advancedExpressions.expression: there was something evil about ...
advancedExpressions.example: There was something evil about the way the house watched them, its dark windows like hollow, unblinking eyes. （there be something adj. about 句式 + 拟人比喻，营造压迫感）

advancedExpressions.expression: we must not stand by while evil ...
advancedExpressions.example: We must not stand by while the evil of cyberbullying silences our classmates one cruel comment at a time. （we must not stand by while 呼告结构，增强号召力）

advancedExpressions.expression: evil triumphs when good people do nothing
advancedExpressions.example: History teaches a sobering lesson: evil triumphs not because it is strong, but because good people, out of fear or apathy, choose to do nothing. （引用式论断 + not because...but because 因果对比，深化说理）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He was an evil man and did bad things.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Beneath his charming smile lurked an evil so cold and calculating that even his closest friends never suspected the ruin he was quietly plotting. （读后续写·反派揭露）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Beneath...lurked 倒装引出隐藏本质 + 抽象名词化 an evil so...that 结果状语 + 双形容词 cold and calculating 精准刻画 + 定语从句收尾制造悬念

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should fight against evil in society.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is incumbent upon every one of us not merely to condemn the evils that plague our society, but to confront them with action, however small, wherever we find them. （议论文·社会责任）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is incumbent upon sb. to 高级责任句式 + not merely...but 递进 + however small 让步插入 + wherever 引导地点状语从句强化普遍性

classPractice.question: I had to ask myself, "Is there ____ ____ involved in science?" (某种恶)
classPractice.note: 课文原句考点：evil 此处作不可数名词"恶、害处"，前用 some 修饰。

classPractice.question: 取消这次旅行是两害相权取其轻。(用 the lesser of two evils)
classPractice.answer: Cancelling the trip was the lesser of two evils.
classPractice.note: 固定短语 the lesser of two evils = 两害相权取其轻；evil 用作名词。

classPractice.question: There was something ____ (evil / evilly) about the stranger's cold, unblinking stare.
classPractice.note: something 后接形容词作后置定语，故用 evil；evilly 是副词不能作定语。

original_sentence: I had to ask myself, “Is there some evil involved in science?”
readingExamples: I had to ask myself, “Is there some evil involved in science?”
definitionEn:
(1) vt. if a situation or activity involves something, that thing is a necessary part or result of it
(2) vt. to include or affect someone or something in an activity or situation
(3) vt. to make someone take part in something; to cause someone to be connected with an event or activity
(4) vt. (be involved in / with) to be closely connected with something, often in a way that takes time or effort

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 使专注，使全神贯注（be involved in 表示深深沉浸）
uncommonMeanings.example: So involved was she in the unfolding story that she did not hear the bell ring, nor notice that the classroom had long since emptied. （读后续写·专注入迷·倒装）

posExamples.sentence: As the plot thickened, she found herself so deeply involved in the strangers' quarrel that she stepped forward before her mind had even decided to. （读后续写·情节卷入·下意识行动）
I am writing to warmly invite you to get involved in our community's tree-planting programme this weekend, an activity that promises both meaningful labour and lasting friendship. （应用文·邀请信）
Genuine learning involves far more than memorising facts; it demands curiosity, reflection, and the courage to question what we think we already know. （议论文·教育本质）

wordForms.other: 过去分词 involved 可后置作定语：the people involved（相关的人）；the money involved（涉及的钱款）

collocations.translation: 【课件】包含；需要（做某事）——The job involves me/my travelling all over the country.
collocations.example: The job involves me travelling all over the country. （课件原句·包含需要义）

collocations.translation: 【课件】涉及；影响（How many people were involved in the staff cutbacks?）
collocations.example: How many people were involved in the staff cutbacks? （课件原句·涉及影响义）
Parents should involve themselves in their child's education. （课件原句·参与义）
The new album came out of her growing involvement with contemporary music. （课件原句·involvement 名词义）

collocations.translation: 涉及、卷入某事（课文原句：evil involved in science）
collocations.example: I had to ask myself, "Is there some evil involved in science?" （课文原句）

collocations.translation: 需要做某事；包含做某事（involve 后接动名词）
collocations.example: The rescue involved wading through waist-deep floodwater, yet no one hesitated. （读后续写·救援场景）
Whatever your talent, get involved, and together we can make a difference. （应用文·倡议信）
The more she got involved in the volunteer club, the more she realised how much a single pair of willing hands could change. （读后续写·成长感悟）

collocations.translation: 与某人有密切关系（尤指恋爱或牵连）
collocations.example: He was warned not to get involved with such a reckless crowd, but the thrill proved too tempting to resist. （读后续写·人物抉择）
A wise teacher involves every student in the discussion, so that no quiet voice is ever left unheard. （应用文·教学建议）
To make the charity sale a success, we should get the whole neighbourhood involved from the very start. （应用文·活动方案）
It was his personal involvement, not his generous donation, that truly moved the orphans. （读后续写·情感升华）
The counsellor cautioned against becoming too emotionally involved in a case, lest sound judgement give way to sentiment. （议论文·理性与情感）

collocations.translation: 相关人员，牵涉其中的人
collocations.example: Before drawing any conclusion, the headmaster patiently listened to every single person involved in the dispute. （应用文·处理事务）

synonyms.example: Every member is encouraged to participate actively in the weekly debate. （应用文·社团通知）
synonyms.usage: 指主动、公开地'参加'某项活动，常接 in；involve 更强调'被卷入、牵涉'或'内在包含'，主客体关系更灵活。

synonyms.example: The documentary engaged the audience so completely that no one glanced at their phone for a full hour. （读后续写·全神贯注）
synonyms.usage: 强调吸引注意力、使人主动投入（engage in / engage sb），带积极互动色彩；involve 可以是中性甚至被动的牵连。

synonyms.example: Any worthwhile goal entails sacrifice; success without struggle is a story rarely told. （议论文·奋斗主题）
synonyms.usage: 更正式、书面，专指'必然带来、作为必要条件包含'，只用于'事物包含事物'，不用于'使人参与'；involve 在这一义上可通用但语域较低。

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·involve 三种搭配辨析(in/with/doing)
advancedExpressions.expression: be/get involved in sth（涉及/参与某事）| be involved with sb（与某人牵连）| involve (sb) doing sth（包含/需要做某事）
advancedExpressions.example: The job involves travelling; he got involved in the case, and was later found to be involved with the gang. （课件三义辨清：包含需要 / 涉及影响 / 参与）

advancedExpressions.expression: be / get involved in sth / be involved with sb / involve doing sth / involve sb in sth / the people involved
advancedExpressions.example: Once you get involved in the project, you'll find it involves far more coordination than you imagined. （in 表"参与某事"，with 表"与某人牵连"，后接 doing 表"包含做"）

advancedExpressions.expression: involve / entail / require / call for / demand
advancedExpressions.example: Any worthwhile goal involves / entails / requires sacrifice. （功能：表"必然包含、需要"，可替换；involve/entail 后可接 doing）

advancedExpressions.expression: involve (v.) → involved (adj. 卷入的/复杂的) → involvement (n. 参与)
advancedExpressions.example: His deep involvement in the case left him too emotionally involved to judge it fairly. （-ment 构名词，过去分词转形容词）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·so + adj. + that 倒装
advancedExpressions.expression: so involved (in ...) was sb. that ...
advancedExpressions.example: So involved was she in the story that she never heard the bell. （so + 表语提前引起主谓倒装 was she）

advancedExpressions.expression: so involved in ... that + 结果
advancedExpressions.example: So involved was he in comforting the lost child that he forgot his own train was pulling away from the platform. （so...that 倒装前置 + 无私忘我的画面，续写中塑造善良品格）

advancedExpressions.expression: get involved and make a difference
advancedExpressions.example: Whatever your talent, there is a role for you — so get involved, and together we can make a real difference to those in need. （祈使呼吁 + together we can 号召口吻，倡议信结尾）

advancedExpressions.expression: true ... involves not only ... but also ...
advancedExpressions.example: True patriotism involves not only pride in one's country, but also the courage to point out where it falls short. （not only...but also 递进 + 下定义式论断，提升思辨深度）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She was involved in the project and worked hard.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Once she threw herself into the project, she became so deeply involved that late nights blurred into early mornings, and the line between duty and passion quietly dissolved. （读后续写·投入忘我）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Once 引导时间状语从句 + threw herself into 动作升级 + so...that 结果状语 + blurred into 时间流逝意象 + 抽象收尾（line between duty and passion dissolved）

sentenceUpgrade.original: This plan involves a lot of work.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Ambitious as it is, this plan inevitably involves painstaking preparation, close cooperation and no small measure of patience — none of which we should shy away from. （议论文·计划论证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Ambitious as it is 让步倒装 + inevitably 强调必然性 + 三名词短语平行（preparation, cooperation, patience）+ none of which 非限制性定语从句收束态度

classPractice.question: This serious traffic incident ____ ____ ____ ____ ____ ____. (涉及一群年轻人)
classPractice.answer: involves a group of young people
classPractice.note: 【课件原题】involve 表"涉及、牵涉"，主语为单数 incident，谓语用 involves。

classPractice.question: ____ ____ ____ ____ ____ ____ will be under further investigation. (凡是参与这个案件的人)
classPractice.answer: Whoever is involved in the case
classPractice.note: 【课件原题】whoever 引导主语从句作主语；be involved in = 参与、牵涉进（案件）。

classPractice.question: ____ ____ ____ (家务事包括做饭), washing dishes, sweeping and cleaning.
classPractice.note: 【课件原题】involve doing sth = 包含做某事；involve 后接动名词 cooking。

classPractice.question: I had to ask myself, "Is there some evil ____ (involve) in science?"
classPractice.note: 课文原句考点：evil 与 involve 是被动关系，用过去分词 involved 后置作定语。

classPractice.question: The rescue involved ____ (wade) through waist-deep floodwater.
classPractice.note: involve doing sth：involve 后接动名词，不接 to do。

classPractice.question: Whatever your talent, ____ ____ (参与进来) and together we can make a difference.
classPractice.note: get involved = 参与进来；固定搭配，get + 过去分词表状态变化。

translation: 科学的，关于科学的；细致严谨的
original_sentence: The first way in which science is of value is familiar to everyone: scientific knowledge enables us to do and make all kinds of things.
readingExamples: The first way in which science is of value is familiar to everyone: scientific knowledge enables us to do and make all kinds of things.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. relating to science, or using the organized methods of science
(2) adj. done in a careful and systematic way, based on evidence and reason
(3) adj. skilled in or trained in science; involving the rules and methods of a particular science

posExamples.sentence: Hunched over the microscope at midnight, the young girl felt a scientific thrill run through her as the mysterious cells finally revealed their secret under the lens. （读后续写·探索发现·科研热情）
I am writing to recommend that our school set up a scientific research club, where curious minds can design experiments, test ideas, and learn to think like real scientists. （应用文·建议信）
A truly scientific approach to any problem demands that we set aside prejudice, examine the evidence honestly, and follow the truth wherever it may lead. （议论文·理性思维）

wordForms.other: 词族全家桶：science(n.)→scientist(n. 人)→scientific(adj.)→scientifically(adv.)；-ist 表"从事……的人"，-ic 表形容词，-ally 构副词

collocations.example: Scientific knowledge enables us to do and make all kinds of things. （课文原句·节选）
A scientific method teaches us to base every conclusion on data rather than guesswork. （应用文·学习经验）

collocations.translation: 科学精神 / 科学态度
collocations.example: A scientific spirit means never accepting a claim simply because everyone else does. （议论文·品质论证）
Years of patient scientific research finally bore fruit when the vaccine passed its last trial. （读后续写·坚持与回报）
Without solid scientific evidence, even the most confident claim is little more than an opinion in disguise. （议论文·论证方法）
Every great scientific discovery begins with a question that others were too busy to ask. （议论文·创新主题）
Scientific progress has doubled human lifespans, yet it cannot, by itself, teach us how to live wisely. （议论文·科技与人文）
The exhibition traced how scientific inquiry gradually replaced superstition with understanding. （应用文·展览介绍）

synonyms.example: She kept a systematic record of every experiment, so that no observation, however small, would be lost. （读后续写·严谨品质）
synonyms.usage: 强调'有组织、按步骤、成体系'，可用于任何有条理的做法；scientific 特指'符合科学原理/方法'，语义更专。

synonyms.translation: 基于实证的，经验主义的
synonyms.example: The theory sounded elegant, but only empirical testing could tell whether it held true in the real world. （议论文·理论与实践）
synonyms.usage: 专指'基于观察和实验、而非理论推演'，学术语域高；scientific 涵盖面更广，既含实证也含系统方法。

synonyms.example: In the heat of panic, one calm, rational voice can steady an entire crowd. （读后续写·冷静品质）
synonyms.usage: 侧重'合乎逻辑、讲道理'，可用于人的思维态度；scientific 更强调依据证据和科学方法，二者常搭配但侧重不同。

advancedExpressions.expression: scientific knowledge / research / evidence / method / spirit / discovery
advancedExpressions.example: Scientific knowledge grows only through rigorous research, solid evidence and a genuine scientific spirit. （scientific + 抽象名词的高频固定搭配集合）

advancedExpressions.expression: science (n.) → scientist (n. 科学家) → scientific (adj.) → scientifically (adv.)
advancedExpressions.example: A scientist relies on science, thinks scientifically, and defends every claim with scientific evidence. （-ist 构人物名词，-ic 构形容词，-ally 构副词）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·科学严谨的(adj.)
advancedExpressions.expression: scientific / systematic / rigorous / methodical / empirical
advancedExpressions.example: She kept a scientific / systematic / rigorous record of every result. （功能：形容做法"有条理、依据实证"，据侧重替换）

advancedExpressions.expression: a scientific curiosity took hold of sb.
advancedExpressions.example: A scientific curiosity took hold of her, and one question led to another until the whole night had slipped past unnoticed. （抽象名词作主语 + take hold of sb. 拟人化，生动刻画求知欲）

advancedExpressions.expression: cultivate a scientific way of thinking
advancedExpressions.example: I sincerely hope our school can help students cultivate a scientific way of thinking, for it is the compass that guides us through an age of information and misinformation alike. （cultivate...way of thinking + 比喻 compass，建议信升华）

advancedExpressions.expression: scientific ... is a means, not an end
advancedExpressions.example: We must remember that scientific advancement is a means, not an end; its worth depends entirely on the human values that guide its use. （is a means, not an end 警句式论断，凸显思辨层次）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She was interested in science and did experiments.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Driven by a scientific curiosity that no obstacle could dampen, she carried out experiment after experiment, undeterred by failure, until at last the data began to whisper their answer. （读后续写·科研坚持）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Driven by 过去分词短语作状语 + 定语从句 that no obstacle could dampen + experiment after experiment 反复结构 + undeterred by failure 让步插入 + 拟人化收尾（data began to whisper）

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should use scientific methods to solve problems.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is high time that we approached our problems in a truly scientific manner — weighing evidence over emotion, and trusting reason over rumour. （议论文·理性呼吁）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is high time that + 过去式虚拟语气 + truly 强调 + 破折号引出解释 + 双 over 对比平行（evidence over emotion, reason over rumour）押头韵增强气势

classPractice.question: ____ ____ (科学知识) enables us to do and make all kinds of things.
classPractice.note: 课文原句考点：scientific 作定语修饰 knowledge；knowledge 不可数，作主语谓语用单数 enables。

classPractice.question: A real ____ (science) must think ____ (scientific), basing every claim on evidence.
classPractice.note: 词族转换：a real 后接名词 scientist（人）；think 后用副词 scientifically 作状语。

classPractice.question: Only through rigorous ____ (scientific / science) research can such a claim be verified.
classPractice.note: 修饰名词 research 需用形容词 scientific；science 是名词不能直接作定语于此。

translation: n. 赞扬，认可；信用 | vt. 存入金额；把…归于
original_sentence: Of course, if we make good things, it is not only to the credit of science; it is also to the credit of the moral choice which led us to good work.
readingExamples: Of course, if we make good things, it is not only to the credit of science; it is also to the credit of the moral choice which led us to good work.
definitionEn:
(1) n. praise, approval or honour that you give someone for something good they have done
(2) n. an arrangement to buy goods or services and pay for them later; the money lent to you in this way
(3) vt. to add an amount of money to a bank account
(4) vt. to believe that someone or something has a particular good quality or has done something good; to attribute something to a source

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】(影视片尾)演职人员字幕（the credits = the list of all the people involved）
uncommonMeanings.example: The credits seemed to last almost as long as the film! （课件原句·片尾字幕义）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （大学的）学分
uncommonMeanings.example: One more credit was all that stood between her and the diploma she had bled four years to earn. （读后续写·大学奋斗·目标在望）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 相信，认为……是真的（常用于否定/疑问）
uncommonMeanings.example: She could scarcely credit her own eyes: the shabby beggar she had helped yesterday now stood before her in a general's uniform. （读后续写·意外反转·难以置信）

posExamples.sentence: When the team lifted the trophy, the quiet captain stepped back and gave all the credit to his teammates, insisting that victory had been a gift they built together. （读后续写·谦逊品格）
On behalf of the whole class, I would like to give full credit to Mr Li, whose patient guidance turned our clumsy rehearsals into a performance we can all be proud of. （应用文·感谢信）
History often credits a single genius with a discovery, yet behind every breakthrough stand countless unnamed hands whose labour made it possible. （议论文·团队与个人）

idioms.idiom: give credit where credit is due
idioms.translation: 该表扬的就表扬；实事求是地予以肯定
idioms.example: However fierce their rivalry, the coach always gave credit where credit was due, praising his opponents' skill without a trace of envy. （读后续写·体育精神·大度）

idioms.idiom: do sb credit / do credit to sb
idioms.example: The way the young volunteers comforted the frightened children does them great credit. （应用文·活动表彰）

idioms.translation: 值得赞扬的是；这是某人的功劳
idioms.example: To her credit, she owned up to the mistake at once and set about putting it right. （读后续写·担当品质）
It was mean of him to take all the credit for a project the whole team had toiled over. （读后续写·人物负面刻画）

collocations.phrase: to the credit of sb / to one's credit
collocations.translation: 【课件】某人值得称赞；归功于某人
collocations.example: To his credit, Jack never told anyone exactly what had happened. （课件原句·归功/值得称赞义）
He's a player who rarely seems to get the credit he deserves. （课件原句·赞扬认可义）
He's a player who rarely seems to get the credit he deserves. （课件原句·deserve credit）

collocations.translation: 【课件】三个学分（credit 作"学分"义）
collocations.example: My math class is worth three credits. （课件原句·学分义）

collocations.translation: 【课件】(影视)演职人员字幕（= the list of all the people involved）
collocations.example: The credits seemed to last almost as long as the film! （课件原句·字幕义）

collocations.phrase: credit A with B = credit B to A
collocations.translation: 【课件】把 B 存入 A；把 B 归功于 A（vt. 存入金额/归功）
collocations.example: $50,000 has been credited to your account. （课件原句·存入金额义）

collocations.translation: 【课件】被认为具有……的功劳；……是某人的功劳
collocations.example: The company is credited with inventing the industrial robot. （课件原句·归功于某人）
$50,000 has been credited to your account. （课件原句·被归功/存入）
The cheetah is generally credited as the world's fastest animal. （课件原句·be credited as）

collocations.phrase: to the credit of sb / sth
collocations.translation: 归功于……；是……的功劳（课文原句）
collocations.example: If we make good things, it is not only to the credit of science; it is also to the credit of the moral choice. （课文原句·节选）
It was mean of him to take all the credit for a project the whole team had toiled over. （读后续写·人物负面刻画）

collocations.translation: 把功劳归于某人；称赞某人
collocations.example: We must give credit to the countless nurses whose quiet devotion carried the city through its darkest months. （议论文·致敬平凡英雄）

collocations.translation: 值得称道的是；这是某人的功劳
collocations.example: To his credit, the young man returned the lost wallet without expecting a single word of thanks. （读后续写·诚实品格）
Modest, hardworking and kind, she is a credit to the school that raised her. （应用文·人物评价）
He slid his credit card across the counter, only to be told, to his embarrassment, that it had been declined. （读后续写·尴尬时刻）
She never sought to take the credit; the smiles on the children's faces were reward enough. （读后续写·无私奉献）
Anyone who dares to admit a mistake and learn from it deserves credit, not ridicule. （议论文·成长心态）
Unable to pay in full, the struggling farmer bought the seeds on credit, staking next year's harvest on a single hopeful gamble. （读后续写·困境抉择）

collocations.phrase: credit sth to / credit sb with sth
collocations.translation: 把……归功于；认为某人具有（某优点）
collocations.example: The historian credited the town's survival to the courage of a handful of ordinary citizens. （议论文·历史评价）

synonyms.example: The teacher's warm praise lit a spark in the shy boy that no scolding had ever managed to. （读后续写·鼓励的力量）
synonyms.usage: 指用言语公开夸奖，是具体的赞美行为；credit 更侧重'把功劳/荣誉归于某人'，含'认可其贡献'之意，比 praise 更正式。

synonyms.example: After years of thankless toil, the old craftsman finally received the recognition his artistry had long deserved. （读后续写·迟来的认可）
synonyms.usage: 指公开承认某人的价值或成就（常搭 receive/gain）；credit 强调'把成绩归于某人'的归属判断，二者可互换但侧重不同。

synonyms.example: It was a great honour to be chosen to represent our province in the national competition. （应用文·发言稿）
synonyms.usage: 语气最庄重，指崇高的荣誉或敬意；credit 偏日常，指对具体贡献的肯定，不像 honour 那样带仪式性。

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·credit A with B = credit B to A(归功/存入)
advancedExpressions.expression: credit sb/sth with sth ↔ credit sth to sb/sth；被动 be credited with / be credited to / be credited as
advancedExpressions.example: The company is credited with inventing the robot; equally, the invention is credited to the company. （课件核心结构：主动两式 + 三种被动，一次记牢"归功"义）

advancedExpressions.type: 短语群·credit(高频多义,一次记牢)
advancedExpressions.expression: to the credit of / give sb credit for / take the credit / to one's credit / a credit to sb / on credit / credit card
advancedExpressions.example: To her credit, she gave all the credit to her team, though the whole idea was a credit to her alone. （表"功劳"的四种句式 + 表"信用"的 on credit / credit card 一网打尽）

advancedExpressions.expression: credit / praise / recognition / honour / acclaim
advancedExpressions.example: The old craftsman finally received the credit / recognition / acclaim his artistry deserved. （功能：表"认可、赞誉"，可替换；credit 侧重"归功"，honour 最庄重）

advancedExpressions.expression: credit (n./v.) → creditor (n. 债权人) → creditable (adj. 值得称赞的) → creditably (adv.) → incredible (adj. 难以置信的,同根 cred-"相信")
advancedExpressions.example: His creditable performance was almost incredible for a beginner. （cred- = 相信/信任，-or 构人物名词，-able 构形容词，in- 表否定）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·to one's + 名词 (表结果/态度)
advancedExpressions.expression: to one's credit / to one's surprise / to one's shame
advancedExpressions.example: To her credit, she owned up at once. （to one's credit 作句首状语，意为"值得称赞的是"，此类结构还有 to one's surprise 等）

advancedExpressions.expression: give / hand the credit to ... rather than claim it
advancedExpressions.example: Instead of basking in the applause, she handed the credit to the very people the world had overlooked, and in doing so won a respect no medal could confer. （Instead of 对比 + in doing so 结果状语，塑造谦逊高尚形象）

advancedExpressions.expression: the credit for ... belongs to ...
advancedExpressions.example: Much of the credit for the event's success belongs to our tireless volunteers, whose warmth turned strangers into friends. （the credit belongs to 归功句式 + 定语从句抒情，感谢信主体段）

advancedExpressions.expression: credit is due not to ... alone but to ...
advancedExpressions.example: The credit for any nation's rise is due not to a few celebrated leaders alone, but to the silent millions whose everyday labour laid its foundations. （not to...alone but to 对比递进，突出集体贡献的思辨观点）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He got all the credit for the work, though others helped.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Though a dozen unseen hands had shaped the project, it was he alone who stepped into the spotlight to claim the credit — and something in her chest tightened at the unfairness of it. （读后续写·不公与共情）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Though 让步从句前置 + it was...who 强调句 + unseen hands 提喻他人贡献 + 破折号引出心理描写（something in her chest tightened）具象化情绪

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should thank the teachers for our success.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It would be remiss of us not to give due credit to our teachers, whose unwavering faith in our potential carried us further than we ever dreamed we could go. （应用文·感谢信）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It would be remiss of us not to 委婉正式句式（双重否定表强调）+ give due credit 固定表达 + 定语从句 whose unwavering faith + 比较级收尾（further than we ever dreamed）升华情感

classPractice.question: 他把冠军（头衔）归功于全队的共同努力。(用 credit ... to ...)
classPractice.answer: He credited the championship to the team effort.
classPractice.note: 【课件原题】credit B to A = 把 B 归功于 A。课件原文作 "He credited the champion to the team effort."，champion（冠军选手，指人）作被归功之物于逻辑不合，此处"冠军"指"冠军头衔/胜利"，按正确语法应为 championship（或 the title/victory），已据此回填并保留 credit...to... 句式。

classPractice.question: 引进新系统是她的功劳。(用 be credited with)
classPractice.answer: She is credited with introducing the new system.
classPractice.note: 【课件原题】be credited with (doing) sth = ……是某人的功劳；with 后接动名词 introducing。

classPractice.question: 引进新系统是她的功劳。(用 be credited to，同一句另一种表达)
classPractice.answer: The introduction of the new system is credited to her.
classPractice.note: 【课件原题】be credited to sb = 被归功于某人；credit A with B = credit B to A 两种句式互换。

classPractice.question: If we make good things, it is not only ____ ____ ____ ____ science. (归功于科学)
classPractice.note: 课文原句考点：to the credit of sb/sth = 是……的功劳；credit 作不可数名词"赞誉、功劳"。

classPractice.question: The quiet captain refused to ____ (take / give) the credit himself and ____ (took / gave) it all to his teammates.
classPractice.note: take the credit = 居功、自己占功劳；give credit to sb = 把功劳归给某人，二者方向相反。

classPractice.question: ____ his credit, he admitted the mistake at once and set about putting it right.
classPractice.note: 固定句首状语 to one's credit = 值得称赞的是；介词用 To。

translation: adj. 道德的；道义上的；品行端正的 | n. 品行，道德；寓意
original_sentence: Of course, if we make good things, it is not only to the credit of science; it is also to the credit of the moral choice which led us to good work.
readingExamples: Of course, if we make good things, it is not only to the credit of science; it is also to the credit of the moral choice which led us to good work.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. relating to the principles of right and wrong behaviour, and to the difference between good and evil
(2) adj. behaving in a way that is considered good and right by most people; having high standards of behaviour
(3) n. a practical lesson about right and wrong that can be learned from a story or an experience
(4) n. (morals) standards or principles of good behaviour

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 精神上的（支持、鼓励），而非物质或行动上的
uncommonMeanings.example: Though he could offer no money, his quiet moral support meant everything to her on the night before the trial. （读后续写·精神慰藉·患难真情）

posExamples.sentence: Torn between keeping the wallet and returning it, the boy faced a moral choice that would quietly decide the kind of man he was to become. （读后续写·道德抉择·成长关口）
The moral of the old fisherman's tale is simple yet profound: patience, not force, is what finally masters the sea. （读后续写·寓言点题）
A truly educated person, I would argue, is not merely one who is clever, but one who possesses the moral courage to do what is right even when it is difficult. （议论文·教育与品德）

idioms.translation: 道德制高点，道义上的优势
idioms.example: By forgiving the boy who had wronged him, the old man seized the moral high ground without uttering a single word of blame. （读后续写·宽恕的力量）
The moral of the story, the grandmother said with a knowing smile, is that kindness always finds its way home. （读后续写·长辈教诲）

collocations.example: The film quietly reminds us that moral values, once lost, are far harder to rebuild than fortunes. （课件搭配·道德观念）
Whether such experiments should be allowed at all is, above everything, a moral issue. （课件搭配·道德议题）
A society that lowers its moral standards for convenience soon pays a heavy price. （课件搭配·道德标准）

collocations.translation: 【课件】道德感很强（高度发达的道德感）
collocations.example: Even as a child she had a highly developed moral sense, and could not bear to see the weak treated unfairly. （课件搭配·道德感强）

collocations.translation: 【课件】道德上的义务；道义责任
collocations.example: As scientists, they felt a moral responsibility to warn the public of the danger. （课件搭配·道德义务）
He was, above all, a moral person who would rather lose money than break his word. （课件搭配·品行端正）

collocations.translation: 【课件】不讲道德（morals n. 品行、道德）
collocations.example: Young people these days have no morals. （课件原句·morals 名词义）
The moral of the film was that crime does not pay. （课件原句·寓意教益义）
It is also to the credit of the moral choice which led us to good work. （课文原句·节选）

collocations.translation: 故事的寓意 / 教训（moral 作名词）
collocations.example: The moral of the story is that kindness always finds its way home. （读后续写·寓言点题）

collocations.translation: 精神支持，道义支持（非物质上的）
collocations.example: Though he could offer no money, his quiet moral support meant everything to her. （读后续写·精神慰藉）
It takes real moral courage to stand alone for what is right when the crowd shouts otherwise. （议论文·勇气与正义）
The doctor was caught in a painful moral dilemma, torn between honesty and mercy. （读后续写·两难处境）
Sound moral values, once planted in childhood, quietly steer our choices for the rest of our lives. （议论文·品德养成）
We all bear a moral responsibility to speak up when we witness injustice, however inconvenient the truth may be. （议论文·社会责任）
As beneficiaries of society, we have a moral obligation to give something back to those less fortunate. （应用文·倡议书）
A leader who abandons his moral standards for short-term gain soon loses the trust that made him a leader at all. （议论文·领导品格）

collocations.translation: 从……中得出教训 / 寓意
collocations.example: From that painful setback she drew a moral she would never forget: honesty costs less than a lie. （读后续写·教训感悟）

synonyms.translation: 合乎道德规范的，伦理的
synonyms.example: The company faced an ethical question: should profit ever come before people's safety? （议论文·商业伦理）
synonyms.usage: 偏正式/学术，常指与职业、社会公认行为准则相关的'伦理'；moral 更日常，侧重个人内心的是非善恶判断。

synonyms.example: She lived a quiet, virtuous life, asking little for herself and giving much to others. （读后续写·高尚人物）
synonyms.usage: 专形容人品德高尚、有美德，褒义色彩强；moral 既可形容人也可形容'道德的（问题、抉择）'，语义范围更广。

synonyms.example: A righteous anger flared in him at the sight of the strong bullying the weak. （读后续写·正义感）
synonyms.usage: 强调'合乎正义、理直气壮'，有时略带自居正义的意味；moral 是中性的价值判断，不含这层情绪色彩。

advancedExpressions.expression: moral (adj./n.) → morally (adv.) → morality (n. 道德) → immoral (adj. 不道德的) → morals (n. pl. 品行)
advancedExpressions.example: The immoral act shocked everyone: it was morally wrong and showed a total lack of morality. （课件补充 immoral / morality；im- 表否定，-ity 构抽象名词，-ly 构副词，复数 morals 表品行）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·moral 形容词多义(道德的/精神上的/寓意)
advancedExpressions.expression: moral values/issue/standards/responsibility（道德的）| moral support（精神上的，非物质）| the moral of the story（n. 寓意）
advancedExpressions.example: Beyond moral support, the film also carries a clear moral: doing what is right is a moral responsibility we cannot shirk. （课件三义辨清：道德的 / 精神上的 / 名词"寓意"）
